articleTitle: Optimized Capacity Planning for High-Charging Districts with Vehicle-to-Grid Interaction Potential
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: With the rapid rise of the new energy vehicle industry, the electric vehicle charging load has grown significantly, posing severe challenges to the stability of the power grid and the capacity planning of distribution transformers. This paper focuses on areas with a high proportion of charging loads and proposes an innovative approach to optimize the capacity of distribution transformers, aiming to thoroughly explore the potential of vehicle-to-grid interaction.

articleTitle: Solar Panel Defect Detection Based on Improved Lightweight YOLOv8n Model
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: Aiming at the problems of low accuracy, high complexity and poor real-time performance of solar panel defect detection models, a lightweight detection model based on YOLOv8n is proposed. Firstly, the C2f-Faster module is employed to fuse FasterNet Block for extracting crucial feature information while reducing redundant computation through feature streamlining. Secondly, an efficient multi-scale attention mechanism (EMA) is introduced to focus on the extraction of features related to minor defects in the neck layer. Lastly, wise intersection over union (WIoU) loss funtion is incorporated to enhance the model's capabilities in target localization and category classification. Experimental results show that on the public solar panel defect dataset, compared with the benchmark model YOLOv8n, the improved model has the mAP@0.5 increased by 2.3%, the parameter amount reduced by 28.9%and the inference speed increased by 152 frames /s. For the defects of solar panels, the improved model effectively realizes the bidirectional optimization of detection accuracy and lightweight.

articleTitle: Nonconvex Extended Object Tracking Method Based on Set Inversion
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: To address the problem of target tracking under nonlinear bounded measurements, this paper proposes a nonconvex extended object tracking method based on set inversion. The method first establishes a nonconvex extended object model using the adjacency matrix. A tree-structured constraint propagation algorithm then shrinks the node state prediction set and constructs the set inversion problem based on measurement equation constraints. The shrunk set serves as the initial interval for the set inversion algorithm, which is used to solve the set inversion problem to obtain the optimal state intervals of the extended object nodes. Simulation and experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm in tracking nonconvex extended object.

articleTitle: Fixed-Time Adaptive Fuzzy Tracking Control for Longitudinal Dynamic Model of Hypersonic Vehicles with Nonlinear Parametrization
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: This paper studies an adaptive fixed-time output tracking control problem for nonlinearly parametrized hypersonic vehicles. To deal with unknown nonlinearly parametrized dynamics, fuzzy logic systems (FLSs) are used to approximate these nonlinear terms. An adaptive fuzzy control scheme is developed by using a backstepping control method, which ensures that the closed-loop signals are globally ultimately bounded and the tracking errors converge into a small neighborhood of origin within fixed time. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed control scheme.

articleTitle: Design of a Variable Stiffness Continuum Robot for Endoscopic Submucosal Dissection
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: The incidence of gastrointestinal malignant tumors has been showing an upward trend, and endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) has become the preferred surgical procedure for early-stage gastrointestinal cancers in recent years. However, there are numerous challenges in using traditional single-channel endoscopy for ESD. Addressing the issue of limited instrument flexibility and loading capacity due to the confined working environment in ESD, and considering the operational requirements of gastrointestinal endoscopic surgery, this paper proposes an innovative five-degree-of-freedom variable-stiffness continuum robot based on the principle of single-cord force locking. The robot’s base is designed similarly to a gimbal mechanism, allowing adjacent bases to rotate freely around the contact ball. By tensioning the pulling ropes, friction between the bases is increased, achieving the effect of variable stiffness. This paper establishes a kinematic model, and elucidates the working principle of variable stiffness. Experiments verify that the tip of the continuum robot can withstand a radial load of 2.5N and achieve trajectory tracking with small error, demonstrating significant potential for providing flexible operation and robust load capacity in ESD surgery.

articleTitle: Unmanned Boat Pollution Cleanup Based on Outpoint Penalty Functions
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: This paper proposes an algorithm that combines an improved penalty function with a Hamiltonian optimization function to solve the trajectory planning problem of unmanned boat pollution cleaning in an ecological lake. In order to shorten the unmanned boat movement time and trajectory distance, this paper parameterizes and discretizes the time and constructs it as a nonlinear optimization problem over different time parameter segments. In addition, a simple and effective envelope modeling is used to transform the obstacles formed by artificial islands in the ecological lake into inequality constraints. The effectiveness of the method proposed in this paper is verified by experimental simulation. The results show that the algorithm in this paper can complete the contamination cleaning in a shorter movement time with a shorter movement distance and maintain a more stable speed.

articleTitle: Multi-robot Path Planning Based on Improved JPS Algorithm Fused with DWA
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: An enhanced Jump Point Search method is proposed, aiming at the issues of numerous inflection points, easily traversed barriers, and lengthy path search time of the conventional Jump Point Search (JPS) algorithm. First, the cost function in the heuristic of the original JPS algorithm is improved to reduce redundant nodes generated during the search path. This also increases the safety distance between the robot and obstacles, enhancing the path's safety and effectiveness. Secondly, by introducing the Dynamic Window Approach (DWA) for local path planning, the robot gains flexible obstacle avoidance capabilities in dynamic environments. This also results in a smoother path, further improving the obstacle avoidance efficiency and task completion rate of the multi-robot system. Finally, the enhanced JPS algorithm is coupled with the DWA algorithm to allow for real-time sharing of path information and obstacle locations. This enables coordinated movement and division of labor among robots, thereby improving the efficiency and safety of path planning. The simulation experiments show that the proposed fusion improvement algorithm significantly enhances search time, path length, and the number of turning points. This verifies the stable obstacle avoidance capability of the improved algorithm in dynamic environments.

articleTitle: Bipartite Consensus Control for Nonlinear Multiagent Systems With Power Uncertainty under Deception Attacks
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: This article investigates a class of bipartite consensus control problem with actuators under deception attacks. Conventional multi-agent systems require input power to be a known positive integer. We have considered a more general system model for this, which is a multi-agent system with uncertain power, where the output power of each agent is unknown. Considering the problem of unknown direction caused by deception attacks on the system, a special class of Nussbaum functions is introduced, and an adaptive neural control protocol is designed. This protocol not only implements bipartite consensus control, but also ensures that all signals in the system are bounded. The final simulation results verified the effectiveness of the algorithm.

articleTitle: PLS Based Fault Detection and Diagnosis For HVAC Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: Heating, Ventilation and Air Conditioning (HVAC) systems are increasingly popular for improving indoor environments, which results in growing energy consumption of buildings. Once the malfunction of one component in such a system cannot be detected and handled in time, the faults may lead to an increase in energy consumption of the whole system. Even worse, huge economic losses and serious accidents will be caused. Data-based techniques can take full advantage of the vast amounts of available process data generated during HVAC operation. Partial least squares (PLS) is more suitable for handling nonlinear data in HVAC systems compared with traditional methods such as principal component analysis (PCA). However, traditional PLS cannot detect faults timely. Therefore, this paper proposes a method based on rapid iterations of the PLS algorithm to achieve fault detection and diagnosis. This method accelerates the algorithm’s iteration by adjusting convergence bound dynamically and uses the residual contribution rates for fault location. This method is applied to a HVAC model with thirty rooms, established using TRNSYS, to validate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Ultra-short-term photovoltaic power prediction based on multi-source data fusion with FreDF-iTransformer
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: Due to the increasing share of photovoltaic (PV) power generation in the power grid, the accuracy of PV power prediction can substantially affect the efficiency of power dispatch. In order to solve the problem of high-accuracy prediction of PV power, this paper proposes a PV power prediction algorithm based on multi-source data fusion. The method comprehensively considers multiple meteorological factors affecting PV power and enriches the calculation parameters of PV power through the combination of multi-source meteorological data and power data. In addition, the method improves the iTransformer model and further strengthens the model’s ability to extract time series information by introducing the FreDF module. Experimental results with other models on real datasets show that the proposed algorithm has higher prediction accuracy in PV power prediction.

articleTitle: Cooperative pursuit-strategy based on RL for pursuer-evader games
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: This paper presents a learning methodology for multiple pursuers to collaborate in chasing an evader within environments characterized by dynamic obstacles. Leveraging a variational autoencoder framework for the obstacle detection, the multi-agent twin delayed deep deterministic policy gradient algorithm is utilized to train the pursuers, while the deep deterministic policy gradient algorithm is employed to direct the evader, forming a comprehensive learning-based pursuit-evasion model. A decoupled reward structure is implemented to balance cooperative and individual incentives, thereby enhancing learning effectiveness.

articleTitle: A Pedestrian Detection Method for Highways Based on Lightweight FCOS and Hybrid Feature Pyramid Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: With the rapid development of the transportation industry, pedestrian detection algorithms on highway roads have become an important research direction. To solve the problem of a large number of model parameters and a large amount of calculation, this paper proposes a road pedestrian detection method based on lightweight FCOS. In this method, the hybrid feature pyramid networks(HyFpn) is introduced by improving the neck feature pyramid networks, and the lighter mobilenetV3 is used as the backbone network. Experimental results show that the proposed method significantly reduces the size and computational complexity of the model while maintaining high detection accuracy, which is conducive to real-time pedestrian detection on resource-constrained equipment. Compared with the existing methods, the proposed method achieves a better balance between accuracy and speed.

articleTitle: PCA-MD Planetary Gear Damage Identification Method Based on Acoustic Emission Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: In order to study the damage identification of planetary gears in a reducer, a PCA-MD (Principal Component Analysis-Mahalanobis Distance) method for damage identification of planetary gears based on Acoustic Emission (AE) signals was proposed. In this paper, AE signals were collected using a DS5-16C Acoustic Emission instrument and RS-2A piezoelectric ceramic sensors, with a sampling frequency of 3MHz and a preamplifier gain of 40dB. First, a set of AE signals from healthy planetary gears was collected as a reference signal, and damage to the planetary gears was simulated on the experimental platform, collecting AE signals in the damaged state. Then, noise interference in the signals was removed through Empirical Mode Decomposition (EMD), and 13 feature parameters of the denoised AE signals were calculated. Through PCA, the 13-dimensional feature parameters were reduced to 2 dimensions, simplifying the complexity of data processing without losing the original valid information. Finally, the parameters obtained after dimensionality reduction were combined with Mahalanobis Distance (MD) to further establish a method for identifying damage in planetary gears of reducers. The damage condition of the planetary gears was judged by calculating the Mahalanobis distance between healthy and damaged signals. The experimental results showed that the PCA-MD method could identify early damage in planetary gears.

articleTitle: Research on the Application of Joint Frequency Regulation Engineering of Optical Storage Power Station
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: The participation of renewable energy stations in the frequency modulation of the grid has become the development trend of the new power system. This paper takes the optical storage power station as an example, introduces its engineering structure, studies the principle of the optical storage power station participating in the frequency modulation of the power grid, establishes the mathematical model of the primary frequency regulation (PFR) and virtual inertia control of the optical storage power station, and collates the relevant parameter setting and evaluation indicators. Then, based on the engineering application, this paper compares and analyzes the application architecture and optimization logic of the optical storage joint frequency regulation engineering, supplementing the lack of the existing research on the frequency regulation technology and engineering application of energy storage. Next, combined with practical engineering application cases, this paper compares and analyzes the characteristics and optimization measures of optical storage combined frequency regulation. Finally, this paper discusses the shortcomings of the research and thinks about the future research direction.

articleTitle: A Multi-strategy Improved Osprey Optimization Algorithm for UAV path Planning
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: Addressing the challenges of reduced population diversity and susceptibility to local optima in the later iterations of the Osprey algorithm, this paper presents a Multi-Strategy Improved Osprey Algorithm (IOOA). Firstly, Piecewise mapping is employed to initialize the population, providing a robust foundation for global search. Secondly, during the exploration stage, we design an adaptive parameter Levy exploration method based on the fishhawk leader. Additionally, we integrate a random disturbance strategy inspired by trigonometric functions to enhance population diversity and improve global exploration capacity. During the exploring phase, we propose nonlinear control parameters to effectively balance exploration and exploitation, thus decreasing the risk of the algorithm stagnating to local optimum. Additionally, we introduce an update formula based on the positions of elite leaders to expedite convergence. Finally, we conduct simulation experiments and statistical tests on 13 benchmark test functions, comparing the performance of IOOA with seven popular algorithms. Simultaneously, we apply IOOA to the UAV path planning problem to validate its optimization performance in practical scenarios. The results indicate that IOOA exhibits faster convergence speed and higher effectiveness compared to other optimizers.

articleTitle: Trajectory Generation for Wheel-Legged Robot Jumping Based on Maximum Torque Minimization
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: This paper proposes a method for optimizing the jump trajectory of a robot, aiming to minimize the maximum torque. By utilizing the dynamics of the entire machine and iteratively refining the range of joint torques, the maximum torque during the jump is effectively reduced. Validation was conducted on a self-developed wheeled-legged robot, and the results show that the generated trajectory is effective and reliable. This method significantly improves the robot’s jumping performance and has important implications for the motion planning of wheeled-legged robots.

articleTitle: Instance Segmentation Based Non-Destructive Inspection of High-voltage Cable Defects
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: The defect inspection of high-voltage cable is an important guarantee for the safe operation of cable. Traditional manual inspection is complex and costly. To solve this problem, this research combine X-ray NDT(non-destructive testing) with deep learning to propose an edge refinement mask network to improve the efficiency and accuracy of cable defect inspection. Specifically, in order to improve the accuracy of network inspection, this research employ a variety of data enhancement methods to extend the X-ray image dataset. For the cable defect edge, this study add the edge refinement operation after the basic example segmentation model, so that the segmented defect edge is more realistic.The experimental results show that the network defect detection accuracy proposed in this study reaches 91.6% and the detection speed reaches 54.7fps. Compared with the general defect inspection methods, the method in this paper has a greater improvement in accuracy and convenience.

articleTitle: Enhancing Safety and Reliability of LNG Receiving Terminals through Data Security Monitoring Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: This article presents a comprehensive analysis of the safety issues associated with LNG receiving terminals, which play a crucial role in the natural gas supply chain. Given the rapid growth of the LNG industry, ensuring the safe operation of these terminals has become a matter of paramount importance. The paper begins by introducing the process flow and highlighting existing safety concerns related to LNG receiving terminals. Subsequently, it proposes the implementation of a data security monitoring platform specifically designed for LNG receiving terminals, and explores key technologies for digital monitoring and intelligent operation and maintenance. Notably, this study focuses on equipment prediction maintenance technology and rollover prognosis technology, both of which contribute to the safe and stable operation of LNG receiving terminals. The findings presented in this paper are expected to significantly enhance safety, reduce accidents, and improve the overall efficiency of LNG receiving terminals.

articleTitle: Hybrid Chaos Mapping Improved Grey Wolf Optimisation Algorithm for UAV Path Planning
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: For the problem of path planning of unmanned aerial vehicles in a three-dimensional environment, this paper proposes a fusion chaos mapping improved gray wolf optimization algorithm. The position update function in the gray wolf algorithm is improved, which is more conducive to the transformation between the exploitation stage and the exploration stage of the wolf pack. The improved Sigmoid function is used as the nonlinear convergence factor to balance the global search and local search of the algorithm. In the chaotic mapping method, Tent chaotic mapping is used for population initialization, which improves population diversity, solution accuracy and convergence speed. Through tests on 8 CEC benchmark functions, this algorithm converges faster and has higher accuracy than the comparison algorithms. In the experimental simulation in the simulated mountain environment, among HTGWO, PSO, GWO and several variants of GWO, the path planned by the HTGWO algorithm has a low threat cost, is smooth and has fewer turning points.

articleTitle: A fixed-time stable underwater manipulator time-varying delay teleoperation system with input saturation
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: In this paper, we consider the problem of bilateral teleoperation of underwater manipulators with time-varying delay, input saturation, and system stability that can be achieved at a fixed time. A non-general prescribed performance function is added to the terminal sliding surface and a virtual system is introduced to overcome the difficulties caused by actuator saturation. Based on the terminal sliding surface, a control scheme is designed to achieve the prescribed performance of position synchronization and virtual error. The stability of the system is proved using the barrier Lyapunov function theory, and a fixed bound on the global settling time is further calculated. Finally, the feasibility and effectiveness of the scheme are verified by simulation experiments.

articleTitle: An Informativity Approach for Data-Driven Distributed Control for Multiagent Systems with Heterogeneous Control Gains
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: This paper investigates the distributed data-driven consensus problem for discrete-time leader-following multiagent systems (MASs) under external disturbances. To reduce the reliance on global information, two nested double-layer observers are proposed to estimate the leader’s state trajectory. According to the estimation, a local data-driven controller is proposed using the informativity approach. Compared with the existing prior work, the proposed observer-based scheme allows followers to use heterogeneous control gain matrices, thereby eliminating the requirement to solve centralized data-driven inequalities and enhancing the distributed characteristics. The effectiveness of the theoretical results are verified through numerical simulations.

articleTitle: End-to-end Object Detection System Using Multi-Source Data Fusion for Autonomous Driving
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: With the rapid development of autonomous driving, modern vehicles are equipped with multiple sensors. Data from these various sensors assist and cross-reference each other, enhancing autonomous driving capabilities. However, the efficient and cost-effective utilization of the vast amounts of data generated by these sensors remains a significant challenge. This study presents an end-to-end multi-source data object detection system based on the YOLOv8 model. By introducing the Pixel Cluster Rotation (PCR) and hint layer, the system enables the fusion of multi-source data without significantly increasing resource requirements. Evaluations show that compared to vision-only object detection, these methods allow the fusion of LiDAR and RGB data with approximately 0.38% additional neural network parameters, resulting in a 2.9% increase in the system's mean Average Precision (mAP). This research can be applied to low-cost platforms with limited system resources, promoting the broader adoption of autonomous driving technology.

articleTitle: Point-line RGB-D SLAM Algorithm Based on Multiple Back-projection Strategy
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: To overcome the limitations of the application of the SLAM algorithm, which is based on point features under harsh conditions, this paper innovatively proposes a SLAM algorithm that is based on point and line feature fusion. The algorithm uses an RGB-D camera as an input sensor to extract feature points and feature lines simultaneously from the input RGB image. To fully exploit spatial line feature information and mitigate the impact of environmental noise, we propose a multiple back-projection strategy guided by a depth map to robustly recover spatial line information. Finally, the proposed algorithm is compared with the ORB-SLAM2 algorithm in the public dataset TUM RGB-D. The results show that the proposed algorithm significantly improves the accuracy of localization and mapping.

articleTitle: An Online Strategy for Nonlinear Vector Autoregression
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: Nonlinear vector autoregression (NVAR), as an effective alternative to traditional reservoir computing (RC), has garnered significant attention in the field of time series prediction in recent years. Unlike conventional RC, NVAR does not require the use of random sampling matrices to define the underlying recurrent neural network, and it features fewer hyperparameters. However, NVAR is an offline model, making it challenging to meet the real-time monitoring requirements of industrial processes. Inspired by the Woodbury matrix identity, this paper proposes an online NVAR that can update the model using data arriving in blocks. Subsequently, this study constructs a soft sensing model based on the online NVAR to perform real-time monitoring of industrial processes. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is validated using a real-world dataset from a wastewater treatment plant.

articleTitle: Enhancing Time Series Prediction in Industrial Processes: A Self-Attention BiLSTM Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: The development of data-driven soft sensors for modeling complex data, particularly in scenarios characterized by strong nonlinearity, high dimensionality, cross-correlation and autocorrelation, remains a significant challenge in process data analysis. Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) networks are highly effective in capturing both forward and backward dependencies within sequences, thereby enhancing the extraction of temporal features from time series data. However, BiLSTM networks may struggle to capture global dependencies, especially in long sequences. To address this limitation, the self-attention mechanism, which excels in modeling global relationships across all positions in the input sequence, can be integrated with BiLSTM by applying weighted attention to the two different directions of BiLSTM, thereby enhancing its performance. This study proposes a novel method called SA-BiLSTM, which combines the strengths of the BiLSTM network and the self- attention mechanism. The self-attention layer captures global dependencies, while the BiLSTM layer extracts comprehensive temporal features in both directions, which are then passed to a fully connected layer for final prediction. Extensive comparisons with traditional methods such as BiLSTM, LSTM with added self-attention mechanism, LSTM, RNN, and SVM validate the superior performance of the proposed SA-BiLSTM method in handling complex time series data.

articleTitle: Autonomous Obstacle Avoidance for UUV Based on Global Guidance Vector Field and Local Particle Swarm Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: Global trajectory planning and autonomous obstacle avoidance for unmanned underwater vehicles (UUVs) are crucial but difficult in unknown underwater environments. The paper proposes a comprehensive and efficient methodology, consisting of global planning with guidance vector field (GVF) and local autonomous obstacle avoidance with particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm. The initial GVF are first constructed based on pre-known currents and static obstacles, to guide an UUV to the destination or tracking a moving target along the shortest trajectory. In order to avoid unknown obstacles, the UUV must be equipped with forward-looking sonars (FLS) or other sensors processed in real time to provide obstacle detection information in the horizontal planes. The local PSO algorithm is introduced to modify the guidance vector field to guide UUV avoiding unknown obstacles safely. Finally, simulation results clearly demonstrate the proposed methodology enables UUVs to safely pass through obstacles in unknown environments.

articleTitle: ES-MSCNN: An Echo State Multi-Scale Convolutional Neural Network for Multi-Step Prediction of Wastewater Quality Variables
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: Given the limitations of hardware sensors together with strong nonlinearities and nexus between variables in wastewater treatment processes (WWTPs), the measurement of key quality variables is usually inaccurate or even impossible. Moreover, due to the short data sampling period, the single-output single-step prediction model cannot meet the actual demand. Therefore, this paper proposes a new soft sensor, termed as the Echo State Multi-Scale Convolutional Neural Network (ES-MSCNN), designed for accurate multivariate multi-step prediction. ES-MSCNN first generates an echo state representation (ESR) containing temporal information through an echo state network (ESN). Subsequently, a convolutional neural network (CNN) is employed to avoid the shallowness of ESN and further extract high-dimensional feature information from the data. Besides, a multi-scale learning strategy is used in the convolutional module to capture multi-timescale features and improve the multivariate prediction accuracy. Validation on the benchmark simulation model 2 platform and comparison with several models indicate that the proposed ES-MSCNN has higher accuracy and stronger robustness in multi-step prediction tasks with multi-input and multi-output.

articleTitle: CETSP-based Trajectory Planning for Redundant Manipulators
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: The trajectory planning problem for redundant manipulators is studied, where the DOF (degree of freedom) of the manipulator is larger than 6. The end-effector is constrained to visit a series of task areas, similar to the Close-Enough Traveling Salesman Problem (CETSP). However, the multiple inverse solutions of redundant manipulators must be considered. This paper proposes an improved genetic algorithm with the simultaneous introduction of three different types of genes. Each chromosome contains three parts, including the order of task areas, the sequence of joint configurations, and the unknown coefficients to be optimized. Numerical simulations are carried out to validate the proposed method. The results show that the end-effector of redundant manipulator accurately visits all task areas.

articleTitle: Modeling of High Speed Maglev Operation Control System Based on AADL
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: AADL is a formal modeling language for real-time embedded systems. This paper compares the differences between different formal modeling methods, introduces AADL modeling method into the field of high-speed maglev to model the operation control system(OCS) of high-speed maglev, and accurately describes the structure of each subsystem of OCS and the information interaction process between subsystems. This paper solves the problem that the conventional formal modeling method is insufficient to describe the system structure by OSATE tool.

articleTitle: Health Status Estimation of Aircraft Engines Based on Clustering and Bi-LSTM with Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: Accurate health status estimation is one of the key technologies to ensure the safe operation of aircraft engines. To improve the accuracy of estimating the health status of aircraft engines, a health status estimation model based on clustering and bidirectional long short-term memory (Bi-LSTM) network with attention mechanism is proposed. On the one hand, attention mechanism is incorporated into the Bi-LSTM network to allow the model to dynamically focus on important information at different positions in the sequence when processing it, thereby improving the model’s understanding ability of the sequence. On the other hand, fuzzy C-means (FCM) clustering algorithm is used to automatically partition the health status of multi-dimensional sensor signals in aircraft engines, to reduce the burden of manual labeling. Finally, the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed model are validated on the C-MAPSS public dataset.

articleTitle: A NOA-AP based Typical Process Route Automatic Discovery Approach for Intelligent Manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: With the continuous advancement of intelligent manufacturing, the efficient extraction of reusable typical process routes based on artificial intelligence for computer-aided process planning (CAPP) has emerged as a critical necessity. Because a good process route can not only effectively improve the efficiency of process planning, but also promote the transformation of traditional manufacturing to intelligent manufacturing. To address this situation, this paper proposes a Nutcracker Optimization Algorithm (NOA) enhanced Affinity Propagation (AP) algorithm under the consideration of clustering effectiveness to automatic discover the typical process routes from the massive historical data. First, two soft constraints (i.e., quantity constraint and size constraint) are introduced simultaneously in the clustering process to ensure the quality and validity of the obtained typical process routes according to the actual demand. In addition, previous research has emphasized that the selection of preference value and damping factor in the AP algorithm significantly influences clustering outcomes. Hence, NOA is implemented to identify the optimal individual within the search space to determine suitable preference values and damping factors, thereby enhancing the clustering quality of the AP algorithm. The numerical illustration shows that the proposed NOA-AP could improve the clustering quality and discover more representative and effective typical process routes.

articleTitle: Feature Extraction and Fusion for Anomaly Detection Using Hybrid Multi-Scale CNN-Transformer Model
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: This paper explores the challenge of effectively detecting and analyzing human intrusion events using vibration signals from Distributed Fiber Optic Sensors (DFOS) in high speed train security monitoring. A novel Hybrid Multi-Scale CNN-Transformer Model is proposed to capture both frequency-domain and time-domain features from vibration signals. The model employs parallel networks—a multi-scale Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) for frequency-domain analysis and a Transformer network for time-domain analysis. The multi-scale CNN uses different convolution kernels to learn features at various time scales, enhancing its ability to capture diverse signal characteristics. Concurrently, the Transformer effectively models temporal dependencies and long-range relationships in the time domain, capturing sequential patterns and dynamics in the vibration signals. This dual approach aims to enhance signal understanding and analysis by integrating comprehensive information from both domains. It effectively handles the diversity and complexity of signals by capturing latent features even in inconsistent signal conditions. The experimental results show that the proposed method achieves superior classification performance.

articleTitle: Path Planning of Mobile Robot Based on BiLSTM-D3QN Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: Aiming at the traditional deep reinforcement learning algorithms with slow network convergence, poor reward convergence stability, and low path planning efficiency, this paper proposes a BiLSTM-D3QN path planning algorithm based on the DDQN decision model. Firstly, bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM) is introduced to make the network memorable and increase the stability of decision-making, so that the reward convergence is more stable; secondly, the adaptive reprioritization of experience replay based on frequency penalty function is proposed to extract important and fresh data from the experience pool to accelerate the convergence of the neural network. Lastly, an adaptive action selection mechanism is introduced to optimize the action exploration further. Simulation experiments show that the BiLSTM-D3QN path planning algorithm ha 2 fewer inflection points, 0.52s less planning time, and 4.4% higher success rate than the DDQN algorithm, and outperforms the traditional deep reinforcement learning algorithms in terms of the convergence speed of the network, the efficiency of the planning, and the stability of the convergence of rewards. The superiority of the BiLSTM-D3QN algorithm in network convergence speed and path planning performance is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Research on Localization Algorithms for Mobile Robots Based on Laser and Inertial Navigation Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: This paper primarily investigates localization algorithms for mobile robots based on laser reflectors. It proposes an ICP (Iterative Closest Point) laser odometry method based on sparse point clouds from reflectors, which provides motion updates for the particle set. Continuous localization of the mobile robot is achieved through particle filtering. Experimental comparisons indicate that this localization algorithm has high positioning accuracy and strong robustness against abnormal interference.

articleTitle: Finite-time Robust Fault-tolerant Trajectory Tracking Control for QUAVs with Actuator Fault
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: This paper proposed a finite-time robust fault-tolerant trajectory tracking control strategy for quadrotor unmanned aerial vehicles (QUAVs) suffering from actuator saturation, unknown external disturbance and actuator fault. Firstly, robust compensation terms are used to handle unknown external disturbance in position subsystem. On this basis, parameter adaptive method is introduced to remove the adverse effects of actuator saturation in attitude subsystem. Then, a fault detection mechanism is designed to estimate the actuator fault in real time. Subsequently, a finite-time robust fault-tolerant tracking strategy based on backstepping framework are proposed and and the finite-time convergence of all error signals are ensurend. Finally, a numerical simulation result is displayed to validate the effectiveness of the proposed trajectory tracking control scheme for the QUAVs dynamic system.

articleTitle: Inverter Fault Diagnosis based on GASF-Alexnet
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: To tackle the challenge of extracting fault features from Voltage Source Inverters (VSI) under dynamic conditions, this paper introduces a novel fault diagnosis method utilizing GASF-AlexNet. Initially, the Gramian Angular Field (GASF) transformation encodes time-series data into images, enhancing feature visualization and discriminability. Subsequently, an enhanced AlexNet deep learning architecture autonomously extracts critical fault features from these images. Moreover, this study employs an adaptive moment estimation (Adam) optimizer combined with a dynamic learning rate decay strategy to optimize the training process and enhance the model's diagnostic accuracy. Comparative analysis demonstrates that the proposed method exhibits superior fault identification performance and efficiency under various conditions compared to traditional techniques. Experimental results validate the effectiveness and superiority of this method in practical applications.

articleTitle: Zero-sum differential game-based fault tolerant control of 3-DOF model helicopter systems
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: This paper presents a pioneering study that simultaneously addresses the optimal tracking and fault-tolerant control problems for a 3-DOF model helicopter system. Leveraging an optimal FTC approach inspired by zero-sum differential game theory, we explore the intricate dynamics of helicopter systems under both system and actuator faults. Unlike previous work on fault-tolerant control, our study considers the controller and composite faults as adversarial players with "intelligent" strategies in a differential game setting. This novel perspective results in the coupled solutions for the optimal fault-tolerant controller and the worst-case composite faults, posing significant analytical challenges. This work provides a foundation for the optimal design of controllers that achieve desired flight performance even in the presence of nonlinear faults, thereby advancing the robustness and reliability of helicopter systems in operational environments.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of a Novel Humanoid Robotic Arm
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel robotic arm that achieves remote driving of each joint through a specialized transmission design, enabling motors and other drive components to be mounted on the base. This reduces the ineffective load on the robotic arm and improves its motion performance. The arm comprises a base, shoulder joint, elbow joint, wrist joint, and hand. The shoulder and wrist joints utilize 3-degree-of-freedom (3-DOF) 3 Revolute-Revolute-Revolute (3-RRR) spherical parallel mechanisms, connected by a 1-DOF elbow joint, resulting in a total of 7 degrees of freedom. This paper discusses forward and inverse kinematic analysis, and simulation validation of the robotic arm, ultimately demonstrating its human-like motion capabilities and performance.

articleTitle: Bearing Fault Diagnosis with Multi-source Information Fusion and Deep Transfer Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: In the fault diagnosis of bearings in hydropower station units, the information provided by a single sensor is limited, and the dynamic characteristics of the operating conditions vary under different load conditions. To address these issues, this paper proposes a bearing fault diagnosis method that integrates multi-source information with deep transfer learning. Firstly, multi-scale features of the input signals are extracted through a fusion convolution module to ensure the completeness and effectiveness of fault information. Subsequently, channel attention and spatial attention mechanisms are used to retain effective information with minimal data, enhancing the efficiency and accuracy of information fusion. Finally, the fault diagnosis method based on transfer learning effectively copes with detection under different loads. To more comprehensively mine and utilize the hidden features in fault signals, this paper combines vibration and temperature signals to build a bearing fault diagnosis experimental platform, collecting vibration and temperature signals at different speeds to generate a dual-channel dataset. Compared to common domain adaptation methods such as deep correlation alignment and domain adversarial neural networks, the proposed model's fault diagnosis performance under different working conditions is validated. Experimental results show that the proposed multi-source information fusion method performs with higher diagnostic accuracy both under the same and varying working conditions, significantly outperforming traditional methods.

articleTitle: Design and analysis of target-attacker-defender games under limited observations*
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: This paper designs a game control strategy for the target-attacker-defender (TAD) games under limited observations that occur on both sides of the defender and target. Three different cases of TAD games are taken into account: 1) protecting a fixed target, 2) protecting a target moving along a fixed trajectory, and 3) protecting an escaping target. For each case, the pursuit strategy, evasion strategy, and defense strategy are particularly designed based on linear quadratic (LQ) game theory. Furthermore, it rigorously proves that the Nash equilibrium is achieved under the designed strategies. The simulation results verify the rationality of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Experimental Study on the Influencing Factors of Leakage Performance of Hydraulic Motor
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: This study takes a certain brand of hydraulic cycloidal motor as the research object, and analyzes and researches the influence of the brand of hydraulic motor, the viscosity of hydraulic oil fluid, the temperature of hydraulic oil supplying, and the fit clearance of the hydraulic motor rotor to the stator on the leakage of the motor through experiments. The results show that there is a significant difference in the leakage between different brands of hydraulic motors with the same displacement; for the same hydraulic motor, the greater the viscosity viscosity, the smaller the leakage; for the same hydraulic motor, the higher the oil supply temperature, the greater the leakage; for the same hydraulic motor, the greater the clearance between the stator and rotor of the hydraulic motor, the greater the leakage. Therefore, in engineering practice, the evaluation of the leakage performance of hydraulic motors needs to comprehensively consider the effects of oil viscosity, oil temperature and hydraulic motor machining clearance.

articleTitle: Decoupling Analysis of Maglev Variable Stiffness Joints Based on Permanent Magnet
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: Variable stiffness joints, due to their variable stiffness feature, have promising application prospects in fields such as human rehabilitation and military surveillance. However, currently, variable stiffness joints generally have problems of weak nonlinearity and difficulty in decoupling. Based on this and previous related work, the paper proposes a novel maglev variable stiffness joint, which contains permanent magnet repulsion force that provides a nonlinear property similar to that of the human elbow. And through structural and static research, a decoupling analysis method of joint stiffness and rotational angle is proposed. The research not only provides a technical path for the hominine nonlinear characteristics of variable stiffness joints but also provides theoretical support for the subsequent control of maglev variable stiffness joints.

articleTitle: Application of Interpretability-Based Federated Learning to Fault Diagnosis of pumpjacks
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: Fault diagnosis of pumpjacks is crucial in oil extraction, but traditional centralised approaches are no longer applicable due to the challenges of data privacy and decentralised data. Federated Learning (FL), an emerging distributed learning approach, becomes a key technology for the solution by protecting data privacy while allowing multiple parties to share model updates. Although FL approaches protect data privacy, the transparency and interpretability of their model decision-making process need to be improved. To address this problem, we introduce the Logical Reasoning-based Interpretable Federated Learning (LRIFL) approach to enhance model transparency and interpretability. Under the LRIFL framework, each FL client generates logic rules from local data, which are uploaded to the server along with model updates without sharing the raw data. The server integrates these rules using intelligent logic connectors and dynamically adjusts the model weights according to the quality of the data reflected in the rules to ensure the accuracy and fairness of the model. Experimental results show that LRIFL has significant advantages in improving classification accuracy and rule fidelity, and is especially suitable for application scenarios with high data privacy and interpretability requirements.

articleTitle: Fusion of Octave and Dilated Convolutional Networks for Enhanced Dense Crowd Counting
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: Accurate crowd counting is crucial for numerous applications ranging from public safety to urban planning. However, existing methods often struggle to adequately capture both fine-grained frequency-domain information and broader semantic context cues, limiting their performance in accurately estimating crowd density. To overcome these problems, we propose a novel method that harnesses the strengths of octave convolutions and dilated convolutions. Octave convolutions effectively decompose features into high-frequency and low-frequency components, focusing on detailed textures of the crowd distribution. Meanwhile, dilated convolutions expand the receptive field without increasing number of parameters, and enable our model to capture rich semantic context for crowd estimation. The experimental results demonstrate that our approach can achieve precise crowd counting by jointly learning frequency-based details and semantic information. Extensive experiments show that the proposed method achieves the competitive performance on ShanghaiTech datasets for crowd counting.

articleTitle: Model Predictive Control of "PV+ESS" Electric Spring
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: This paper introduces a new Electric Spring topology-Photovoltaic and Energy Storage System Electric Spring. On the basis of the common topology electric spring-2(ES-2), the power supply that provides DC bus voltage is changed to photovoltaic power,and the bus voltage stability is adjusted by a double-closed loop. And, the voltage stability of the control critical load is realized by Finite Control Set Model Predictive Control(FCS-MPC). Finally, the feasibility of the proposed scheme is verified by simulation and experiment platform. On the basis of realizing the original function of the Electric Spring, the photovoltaic energy utilization rate is further improved.

Author Keywords: photovoltaic and energy storage system electric spring

articleTitle: An Overview of Methods of Industrial Anomaly Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: Industrial anomaly detection plays a crucial role in modern manufacturing and production processes. In order to help researchers and professionals in the manufacturing industry understand the developing research results in this field, this paper begins with an introduction of common methods of industrial anomaly detection such as neural networks, GAN, transformer with discussing the limitations in this domain. Subsequently, owing to the emergence of the fourth wave of artificial intelligence, Advanced anomaly detection techniques based on Large Language Models (LLMs) and variants are explored, including AnomalyGPT, VisionGPT and LLMAD which have influenced a lot as the cutting-edge technologies. Additionally, based on the current developing trends of the LLMs-based method, this paper analyzes challenges and deficiencies existing in practice which have the potential to lead the way in future research. Conclusively, this overview exposes the bottleneck of traditional methods and emphasizes the revolutionary impact LLMs could have on multimodal scenes of anomaly detection while putting insight into the extend of methodical practicability.

articleTitle: Modeling and Control of Magnetic Gap in Lorentz Force Maglev Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: The Lorentz force magnetic platform, as a new generation of high-precision turntable for magnetic levitation satellites, can meet the requirements of ultra-high attitude pointing accuracy and attitude stability for future spacecraft. To solve the multi-body attitude control problem under maneuvering conditions, the dynamic modeling of three types of magnetic bearings is first based on the equivalent magnetic circuit method, and the magnetic gap is finely modeled based on the relative poses of the magnetic levitation module and the payload module. Secondly, design a multi closed-loop control system consisting of radial pose control of the payload module, axial position control of the payload module, and axial attitude control of the payload module, and reverse calculate the magnetic gap changes based on the coupling relationship. The final simulation results verified that under the load centered control method, the magnetic gap variation is stable within a safe range, and the electromagnetic force is stable below the control limit.

articleTitle: State and Disturbance Estimations of Typical Nonlinear Systems in Electromechanical Engineering
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: Taking a single-link flexible system driven by a DC motor as an example, the Takagi-Sugeno (T-S) fuzzy model is used to study the state and disturbance estimation methods for nonlinear systems, which are commonly present in the field of electromechanical engineering. By analyzing the working mechanism of the system, a nonlinear model of the system is established and then expressed as a T-S fuzzy model. By utilizing system state extension, the original system is transformed into a formal generalized system to achieve both system state estimation and estimation of system output disturbances. A robust proportional-integral observer is designed to achieve system state and disturbance estimation. The solution for the observer gain matrix is obtained by solving linear matrix inequalities. The system is studied separately with and without disturbance, and the correctness and effectiveness of the proposed method are verified through simulation results.

articleTitle: YOLOv8-GDI: A lightweight YOLOv8 for real-time Pedestrian Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: Aiming at the current challenges of low detection efficiency in real-time pedestrian detection algorithms, complex model structures, and difficulties in implementing them on mobile devices, we proposed YOLOv8-GDI, a lightweight pedestrian detection model designed based on the backbone of YOLOv8n. Firstly, the C2f-Ghost module is constructed by incorporating the Ghost Convolution in the model, in order to decrease the number of floating-point operations during feature channel fusion and enhance feature expression capability. In addition, Dynamic Task Align Detection Head(DTADH) was designed to facilitate the interaction between the model classification and localization to further enhance the model's detection performance. Finally, the Inner-CIoU loss function was introduced into the YOLOv8n to improve the ability to localize features of different sizes. The experimental results show that compared with YOLOv8n, YOLOv8-GDI reduced the number of parameters by 50%, decreased the computational complexity by 25%, and maintained a high detection accuracy on the Wider person dataset. This suggested that the improved model is more lightweight and has better application value in the direction of real-time pedestrian detection.

articleTitle: Dynamic Temporal Convolutional Networks for Fault Diagnosis of Rolling Bearings
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: Since rolling bearing plays a crucial role in rotating machinery, the fault diagnosis research of it has been widely concerned in recent years. However, the collected fault signals often contain a lot of noise interference due to the complex and changeable operating environment. The anti noise capability of traditional deep learning methods is weak, resulting in poor feature extraction performance. Therefore, the dynamic temporal convolutional network (DyTCN) is presented for rolling bearing fault diagnosis in this article. Specifically, the causal dilation convolution is first designed to acquire fault feature of vibration signal by enlarging receptive field of the network. Then, the dynamically adjusted convolution kernel parameters are used to achieve adaptive acquisition of dynamic features and improve the robustness. Extensive experimental results on real dataset demonstrate that DyTCN has excellent accuracy in fault diagnosis.

articleTitle: Output Cluster Synchronization of Heterogeneous Networks via Pinning Control
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: This paper studies an output cluster synchronization problem of heterogeneous networks. Based on the internal model principle, heterogeneous networks are transformed into networks with a heterogeneous layer and a virtual nonidentical layer. By means of pinning control, a novel output cluster synchronization strategy is proposed. Three algebraic and graphic conditions are derived to specify control parameters. It is shown that the outputs of agents in heterogeneous networks are synchronized according to the clusters as long as fewer agents are pinned. Compared with the existing results, cluster tracking can be further achieved and control parameters can be always determined no matter how the magnitudes of coupling strengths among agents vary. Application cases on heading cluster synchronization of heterogeneous ships are provided to verify the effectiveness of theoretical results.

articleTitle: Cooperative Navigation for UAV Swarm Based on Gaussian Particle Belief Propagation
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: Cooperative navigation realized through information interaction among UAVs can improve the navigation performance of UAVs in complex environments. In this paper, we construct a distributed cooperative navigation framework that fuses measurements from various onboard navigation sensors and inter-UAV ranging. Considering the computational efficiency, we propose a Gaussian particle filter for message passing and computation, which reduces the computational load. Flight test results show that the algorithm can significantly improve the computational efficiency with the same positioning accuracy compared to the traditional BP algorithm.

articleTitle: A Depth-Estimation Approach Enabling Closed-Loop Control of Water Surface Gliding
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: Aerial-aquatic unmanned vehicle(AAUV) is a new class of vehicles capable of operating in multiple domains, specifically in the air and water. These vehicles can glide on the water surface using onboard hydrofoil. Accurate depth measurement is required to ensure closed-loop control of its water surface gliding. Existing methods of measuring water depth usually use a single sensor so that accuracy could be improved, but some methods are not suitable for mounting on autonomous vehicles. To address the above problems, a fusion method based on adaptive weighting and Kalman filtering is designed to make the final depth results more accurate. The accurate depth measurement obtained during AAUV gliding ensures stability during the process. Compared with a single pressure sensor using only the Kalman filter, the average error of the fusion result is reduced by 53.1%, and the maximum error is reduced by 61.6%. Experimental results show that the proposed algorithm is easy to implement and improves accuracy and stability.

articleTitle: Smart Flexible Wrist Exoskeleton with Twisted String Actuators and IMU Feedback
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: As technology advances, there is a growing demand for lightweight and cost-effective rehabilitation and wearable devices. Traditional metal and pneumatic actuators are increasingly unable to meet modern requirements due to their bulk and high cost. In contrast, twisted string actuators (TSAs) present an ideal solution, offering high efficiency, low cost, and ease of fabrication. In this study, a smart, flexible wrist exoskeleton powered by TSAs was designed and fabricated. By analyzing the relationship between TSA output force, motor rotations, and motor voltage, we achieved precise control of the wrist’s three degrees of freedom. The exoskeleton supports a range of motion including wrist flexion and extension (122°), adduction and abduction (61°), and pronation or supination (86°). Additionally, two nine-axis Inertial Measurement Units (IMUs) were employed to acquire real-time wrist orientation data, which was visualized using UPBGE software, enhancing the device's interactivity. Experimental results demonstrate that the TSA-driven smart flexible wrist exoskeleton excels in portability, cost-effectiveness, and adaptability, making it suitable for a wide range of applications.

articleTitle: Neural-network-based Adaptive Fault-tolerant Control of Switched Nonlinear Systems with Full State Constraints
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: This paper studies the adaptive fault-tolerant control problem for switched nonlinear systems with full-state constraints and unknown functions. To address this challenge, radial basis function neural networks (RBFNNs) are utilized for function approximation, barrier Lyapunov functions (BLFs) are applied for ensuring constraint adherence, and the backstepping technique is employed for systematical control design. The combination of these methods is relatively novel, and on this basis, actuator faults are compensated. It is demonstrated that all closed-loop signals are globally bounded with the tracking error confined within a predefined compact set.

articleTitle: Concrete Roughness Grade Identification Based on the Improved AlexNet
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: Because the roughness of the concrete binding surface affects its shear resistance and bond strength, so designing a deep learning model can identify the roughness of the concrete binding surface, which can detect the roughness of the binding surface more intuitively and quickly. First, based on the AlexNet model, we identify the roughness level of the collected depth map of the concrete binding surface, and obtain the deep learning model that identifies the roughness of the main network. Later, the recognition accuracy of the model is improved by embedding the attention mechanism behind the convolutional layer of AlexNet in three ways. In Method 1, the CBAM channel attention mechanism is embedded behind each convolution layer of AlexNet to obtain the AlexNet_CC model. In Method 2, the CBAM spatial attention mechanism is embedded behind each convolution convolution layer of AlexNet to obtain the AlexNet_CS model. In Method 3, the CBAM attention mechanism is embedded behind each convolution layer of AlexNet to obtain the AlexNet_C model. Through the simulation, the accuracy of the discovery method 3 is better than that of method 1, method 2 and the original network, and the accuracy can reach 95.36%, so the AlexNet_C model can better identify the roughness level of the concrete binding surface.

articleTitle: Visual Analysis of Bacterial Collective Motion
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: In recent years, the patterns and mechanisms of bacterial swarming have inspired the development of novel micro-robots that can mimic the behavior of intelligent biological systems, providing greater flexibility and efficiency. This has become a hot topic in the field of microbiology. The analysis of swimming bacterial swarms is currently influenced by various factors, including interactions among individual bacteria, biological characteristics, and environmental conditions. Experimental observations indicate that at high cell densities, bacteria exhibit coordinated movement on a scale of 10 to 100 micrometers. This coordination results in complex flow patterns due to the interactions and feedback between bacteria and the fluid. This paper proposes two methods for analyzing the motion of bacterial populations: the pyramidal Lucas-Kanade (LK) optical flow method and the particle image velocimetry (PIV) method. The LK optical flow method reflects the overall trajectory of the bacterial population, while the PIV method provides a vector map of the velocity of the bacterial swimming. Combining these two methods allows for multilevel analysis of bacterial motion in high-noise, low-contrast videos of swimming.

articleTitle: ILC Coupled with Unscented Kalman Filter Strategy for Trajectory Tracking
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: This paper employs an iterative learning control (ILC) approach to achieve tracking task for non-repetitive time-varying systems (NTVSs). In industrial production tasks, the actual model of the system is usually unknown, and the nominal model will have a certain degree of error, which brings complexity and difficulty to the design of control task. To tackle this issue, ILC framework incorporates unscented Kalman filter strategy to estimate parameter, which yields the proposed algorithm. The robust convergence property of the scheme is proven in theory based on the design goal. Finally, the advantage of the proposed method is demonstrated by comparison with other methods.

articleTitle: A Bearing Fault Diagnosis Method Based on Multimodal Attention Feature Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: This paper proposes a fault diagnosis method based on Multi-modal Attention Feature Fusion (MMAFF). Firstly, a multi-modal processing strategy is introduced, converting one-dimensional vibration signals into two-dimensional image modalities, and extracting features from both signal and image channels. Secondly, the attention mechanism is introduced to integrate the dual path features. Then, the diagnosis framework is obtained through an improved residual block. Finally, the method is tested on the Case Western Reserve University (CWRU) rolling bearing dataset, and cross-condition comparison experiments demonstrate that the proposed method (MMAFF) exhibits good recognition capabilities under different working conditions.

articleTitle: Incremental CBS: Adaptive Multi-Agent Pathfinding in Dynamic Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: In Multi-Agent Pathfinding (MAPF), traditional Conflict-Based Search (CBS) algorithms excel in static environments but struggle with efficiency and responsiveness in dynamic settings. This study introduces the Incremental Conflict-Based Search (ICBS) algorithm, which enhances response efficiency through incremental updates, only adjusting paths for agents affected by environmental changes. By constructing a dependency graph between agent paths and the environment, ICBS quickly identifies necessary path adjustments. A dynamic monitoring module ensures timely responses to obstacle changes. Experimental results show that ICBS outperforms traditional CBS in dynamic scenarios, making it ideal for applications like automated warehouse management and robotic soccer.

articleTitle: Local Linear Fitting Method for Lidar Depth Completion Based on RGB Image Guidance
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: The depth image contains rich spatial information, which is crucial for simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) as well as accurate environmental perception. However, the original depth image is often sparse and contains small holes with missing depth values. In this paper, we have implemented point cloud depth image projection and proposed an RGB image guided completion method. Objects of the same class typically have similar color and depth values. Our local linear fitting method utilizes regions with similar colors to construct a completion objective function. Experiments in both indoor and outdoor scenes demonstrate that our method can generate a depth image with the same resolution as the RGB image. Analysis reveals that our method enhances the quality of depth image completion compared to traditional methods that rely solely on point cloud kernel dilation.

articleTitle: Finite-Time Control for Stochastic Systems with Input and Measurement Powers of Unknown Time-Varying Function Forms
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: This article addresses the finite-time tracking control of stochastic systems with time-varying input and measurement powers. Compared to the existing results with known input powers, the input powers of the system studied in this paper are unknown time-varying functions, which makes the design of control strategy extremely difficult. Additionally, since the signals will deviate during actual measurements, this article also considers the problem of measurement power drifts. To resolve these two problems, this article constructs a new controller by establishing new error variables, which guarantees the finite-time stability of the stochastic system. Finally, the efficiency of the proposed control strategy is confirmed by simulation experiments.

articleTitle: Stability Control of Quadrotor UAV with Manipulator
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: Compared with Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAV), a UAV with a manipulator (UAVM) exhibits significant trajectory deviations. Due to the coupling of the UAV and the manipulator, the stable control of UAVM represents a challenging problem. To address this issue, a PID-based control approach is proposed. First, the dynamics of UAVM is developed using the Euler-Lagrange method. Second, a PID-based controller is designed to achieve stable control of UAVM. Finally, numerical simulations are carried out to verify the proposed approach. Simulation results show that the manipulator accurately track its trajectory while the stability of UAV is achieved.

articleTitle: Design of Haptic Sensing Snake Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: Snake robots, a category of bionic robots, have garnered significant interest due to their capacity to adapt autonomously to complex unstructured environments. This is achieved through the flexibility and versatility of their bodies and gaits, as well as the coordinated movements of their bodies. However, in unknown or complex environments with obstacles, snake robots are unable to plan their next locomotor actions based solely on the sensory information obtained from the camera they carry. The incorporation of haptics is anticipated to facilitate the snake robot's perception of the interaction between its body and the external environment, thereby enabling more precise and effective guidance for efficient movement. This paper presents the design of a flexible tactile sensor based on the principle of photoconductivity, which has been developed to enable a snake robot to perceive and interact with its environment through tactile sensing. The sensor is intended to enhance the robot's autonomous movement capabilities in complex environments where visual recognition or human observation alone is insufficient.

articleTitle: Road Scene Image Segmentation based on Deep Learning and Meta Pruning
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: Semantic segmentation of road scenes is crucial in autonomous driving technology, as it involves identifying and understanding the surrounding environment in real time and accurately, which requires a segmentation network that can process a large amount of image data quickly in real time and accurately distinguish different objects in a complex and changing environment, usually this model is too complex to guarantee real time or too simplified, resulting in a large reduction in accuracy. Existing lightweight models primarily focus on reducing computational load and the number of parameters, but the significance of network parameters to model performance is ignored or difficult to distinguish. To overcome the issue, we propose a novel approach combining deep learning with meta pruning to construct a light weighted road scene segmentation model, The advantage of meta pruning is that it evaluates the significance of different parameters to the network model, retaining the significant parameters and removing the minor ones to achieve precise pruning. The current results show that the method performs well on standard data sets.

articleTitle: Domain Contrastive Alignment Network for Pipeline Fault Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: The general domain adaptation (DA) approach focuses on making the source and target domains of the feature space as close as possible, while ignoring the inter and intra-class distances of the domain samples, leading to poor generalization performance of the model. To tackle this issue, a novel Domain Contrastive Alignment Network (DCAN) algorithm is proposed in this paper, which extracts fine-grained information by minimizing the intra-class distance and maximizing the inter-class distance. The proposed DCAN algorithm is applied to the fault diagnosis of oil and gas pipeline networks to verify its performance, and the results of cross-domain experiments show that the DCAN algorithm effectively improves the accuracy of fault diagnosis in comparison with state-of-the-art algorithms.

articleTitle: LK-ORB-SLAM3: An RGB-D Visual SLAM Algorithm Fusing Optical Flow Tracking and Feature Matching
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: In response to the issue of poor real-time performance caused by the large computational load of feature-based methods, this paper proposed an RGB-D visual SLAM algorithm which integrates optical flow and feature-based methods. This algorithm combined optical flow with the feature-based method, effectively improving the real-time performance of the algorithm while maintaining high precision. Firstly, keyframes are matched using feature-based methods, and camera motion is computed by minimizing the reprojection error. For non-keyframes, keypoints are extracted without computing descriptors and tracked using the optical flow pyramid, and pose estimation is achieved by minimizing the photometric error. Secondly, a dual mechanism based on time and space is employed to execute keyframes insertion which ensures tracking stability. Additionally, an adaptive threshold algorithm is proposed to enhance tracking robustness in low-light environments. Experimental results on the TUM dataset indicated that, with comparable average localization accuracy, the proposed algorithm reduces average tracking cost by 37.19%, achieving real-time frame rates of up to 45 fps on mid-to-low-performance CPUs.

articleTitle: A Distributed Robust Fusion Filter Design with Randomly Occurring Parameter Uncertainty and Sensor Resolutions
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: This paper discusses the distributed fusion (DF) filtering problem for a class of multi-sensor (MS) nonlinear systems undergo randomly occurring parameter uncertainty (ROPU) and sensor resolutions. Among them, the ROPU is considered in the state model. which can be depicted by using the norm-bounded uncertainty and Bernoulli distributed random variable.
