In addition, the sensor resolution that can not be ignored in the process of algorithm design is a basic parameter of the sensor. In this case, the goal of the presented DF filtering issue is that by exploiting the covariance intersection fusion rule, the DF filter is designed. Meanwhile, the local upper bound concerning on the filtering error covariance is presented by using the matrix inequalities and inductive approach, and this upper bound is minimized in terms of choosing the proper filter gain. A numerical simulation is performed to test the effectiveness of the presented fusion method.

articleTitle: Foggy Road Scene Detection Based on Improved Yolov8n
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: In response to the target detection of intelligent systems under foggy conditions, which faces the problem of reduced detection accuracy due to reduced contrast of captured images, color shift and loss of details, a foggy road scene detection method based on improved Yolov8n is investigated. Firstly, the DehazeNet algorithm is combined with the target detection algorithm for defogging to obtain relatively clear images in order to reduce the interference of fog on target detection; Secondly, the Dilation-wise Residual (DWR) module is added to a portion of the C2f module of the backbone network, which enables the network to flexibly adapt to features at different scales to improve the detection accuracy; Finally, the proposed method is tested on the real fog-containing road scene dataset RTTS, and the mAP@50 is improved by 2 percentage points compared with the original model, which validates the feasibility and effectiveness of the design ideas and the proposed method in this paper.

articleTitle: Flight control for helicopter systems under output constraints and stochastic fault factors
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: This article proposes the issue of the helicopter altitude attitude systems with output constraints under stochastic fault factors. The fault factors are described by the switching systems with Markov jump parameters, which enable actuators to operate in different fault modes. Neural networks techniques are used to deal with uncertain inputs triggered by actuator faults. The random fault-tolerant controller is developed for helicopter systems based on the backstepping approach, allowing the control of continuous systems with discrete switching signals. Then, output state constraints are enforced using the barrier Lyapunov function and the tracking errors are proved remain within reasonable bounds via the Lyapunov stability method. Simulation results indicate that the control scheme can maintain the helicopter flight tracking performance under stochastic fault conditions.

articleTitle: Research on Industrial Small Sample Object Data Enhancement Strategy for Robot Vision
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: For the problems of insufficient number of samples and lack of sample diversity faced by industrial scenes in robot vision applications, this paper proposes an improved data enhancement strategy for industrial small-sample objects. The method combines a stochastic algorithm with a deep learning-based image generation technique to generate a large number of realistic real-life style target images from a small number of template images, thus effectively improving the recognition ability of target objects in complex backgrounds. In addition, virtual reality technology is introduced to generate virtual artifact images with similar styles to those captured by actual cameras using a virtual engine, further enriching the diversity and coverage of the dataset. This technique also employs an advanced algorithm that incorporates a convolutional network and a self-attention module in a cyclic adversarial generative network (CycleGan) to achieve efficient generation and style migration of industrial object images. This data enhancement strategy enriches the training data of the robot vision system and significantly improves the robot's stable detection ability and data quality of targets in complex environments.

articleTitle: Optimal Policy Learning for Distributed Formation Control of Behavior-based UAVs
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: This work studies the distributed formation control problem of behavior-based unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). A novel distributed reinforcement learning behavioral control (DRLBC) is proposed to reduce the cost during distributed formation and obstacle avoidance processes. Firstly, a distributed reinforcement learning task supervisor is designed to prevent undesired priority switching between distributed formation and obstacle avoidance behaviors. Subsequently, a reinforcement learning controller is developed to strike a balance between control efficacy and resource consumption. Furthermore, an adaptive sliding mode control law featuring an unknown control input observer is implemented to enhance system robustness. Finally, the simulation results show that the proposed DRLBC drives a group of UAVs to form a distributed formation while avoiding obstacles near their paths.

articleTitle: Event-Triggered Consensus Tracking Control of Nonlinear Multi-Agent Systems with Actuator Faults and Unknown Control Directions
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: In this work, the consensus tracking control problem of leader-follower nonlinear multi-agent systems with actuator faults and unknown control directions is studied. Based on the application of neural network, the uncertain nonlinear dynamics appearing in the analysis process are approximated to attenuate the impact on the system performance. To deal with the unknown control directions in the system, the Nussbaum gain function technique is applied. Moreover, to reduce the communication burden of the system, a class of event-triggered control strategy is designed. Furthermore, a neural network-based on adaptive event-triggered control scheme is proposed to achieve the consensus tracking control of given multi-agent systems with actuator faults. By using the Lyapunov stability theory, the effectiveness of the proposed control scheme is analyzed. The results show that the proposed control scheme not only ensures that the follower agents can track the trajectory of the leader agent, but also proves that the proposed control scheme is not affected by Zeno phenomenon.

articleTitle: Stochastic Resonance in Excitable Gene Regulatory Networks with Gaussian Colored Noise
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: The molecular noise plays an important role in biological systems. In this paper, we investigate the effect of the colored noise in the process of information transfer in the excitable general regulatory model. With the input signals being a random Bernoulli sequence, calculation by an information-based methodology discloses that both the noise intensity induced stochastic resonance and the correlation time induced stochastic resonance might appear. The finding illustrates noise can amplify information transfer. We also find an approximate region where the two kinds of stochastic resonances occur.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Reweighting Method Based on the Effective Area for Fault Severity Classification under Class Imbalance
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: In real-world scenarios, fault severity data follows an imbalance distribution, meaning that normal and low-level faults constitute a large portion of the training data. In contrast, high-level fault instances are relatively scarce. This imbalance leads to the decision hyperplane of classifiers to skew in favor of higher fault levels. Typically, reweighting methods ensure that hyperplanes fairly divide the feature space by assigning weights based on the number of instances. However, we found that the number of instances fails to represent the effective area within a fault level in the feature space. To tackle this issue, we first analyze the distribution and their correlations of different instances within each class. Second, we calculate the effective area by treating instances of the same class as identically distributed random variables. Third, we introduce a novel weighting approach, with weights inversely proportional to the effective area. This method results in more flexible weights, allowing for adaptive adjustments based on feature optimization during the training process. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms the comparative methods on a real-world fault severity dataset and enhances fault diagnosis performance under class imbalance.

articleTitle: Endoscopic Lesion Detection Based on Improved SSD
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: Aiming at the problem of low accuracy and speed of lesion detection by lightweight model, an endoscopic lesion detection algorithm based on improved SSD is proposed. Firstly, the VGG backbone network is replaced with a lighter MobileNetV2 network to reduce the consumption of computing resources. Secondly, the CBAM attention mechanism is proposed to refine the shallow input features, so as to comprehensively capture the key information of the features. Finally, the improved SmoothL1 loss function is used to balance the accuracy and robustness of the model. Experiments show that the average accuracy of the improved model is improved, the parameter amount is 1/6 of the original model, the calculation amount GFLOPS is reduced by 59 G, and the frame rate per second FPS is increased by 96 frames/s. Compared to other algorithms, there is an improvement in average accuracy, the model is more lightweight, and it consumes fewer computing resources, indicating the effectiveness of the improved algorithm in the detection of endoscopic lesions.

articleTitle: Quadcopter Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Formation Trajectory Tracking based on Extended State Observer with Model Predictive Control
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: To address the formation trajectory tracking of Quadcopter Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (QUAV) in the complex environment, this paper integrates a Model Predictive Control (MPC) method with an Extended State Observer (ESO), which effectively solves instability of flight coordination resulting from external disturbances and internal uncertainties. The prediction model of the MPC controller is obtained based on Taylor series expansion and Euler transform. ESO estimates external disturbances and internal uncertainties in real-time, adjusts the desired speed via proportional compensation, thereby achieving precise control of formation trajectories. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method efficiently suppress external disturbances and internal uncertainties, thereby enabling precise tracking of the trajectory for the formation.

articleTitle: Fault-Tolerant Control for a Class of 1-D Systems with Unknown Input Powers and Measurement Drifts
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: This article considers a fault-tolerant control problem for a class of 1-D systems with unknown input powers, actuator failure and measurement drifts. Unlike most current systems where the input power is one or known, the unknown input powers is considered in this article. Based on Lyapunov stability theory, two kinds of controllers are designed, which are suitable for the two cases of whether the system has measurement drift or not. Under the control strategy proposed in this article, the closed-loop system is asymptotically bounded, and all the signals in the system converge to a small neighborhood of the origin. Finally, two numerical examples are given to verify the effectiveness of the control strategy.

articleTitle: RBF Neural Network-Based Adaptive Fault-Tolerant Control of Electromechanical Servo System with LuGre Friction
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: An adaptive control scheme was put forward for electromechanical servo system with LuGre friction, with a view to mitigating the detrimental effect on the system by friction nonlinearity. Initially, the LuGre friction model was presented for the servo system. Through incorporation of sliding mode function, selection of Lyapunov function and development of adaptive law based on a radial-basis-function (RBF) neural network (RBFNN), we designed an adaptive fault-tolerant controller that used RBFNN for electromechanical servo system for the first time, to the best of our knowledge, and assessed its stability. Simulation results showed that our control scheme outperformed the single RBFNN control in both speed and position tracking.

articleTitle: Position Correction and Coordinate System Fusion for Multi-Robot Arm Systems Using Multiple LiDAR Sensors
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of improving the accuracy and robustness of multi-robotic arm coordinate system fusion and position correction using multiple LiDAR sensors. We propose an enhanced adaptive Extended Kalman Filter (A-EKF) that dynamically adjusts process and measurement noise covariances based on real-time sensor data and environmental conditions. The theoretical framework encompasses spatial coordinate transformation, sensor data integration, and error mitigation strategies, ensuring precise harmonization of multisensor data. Convergence analysis demonstrates the stability and effectiveness of the proposed A-EKF, and numerical experiments validate its superior performance over traditional EKF methods, particularly in scenarios with varying noise characteristics. The findings highlight the potential of the proposed method for applications requiring high-precision positioning in dynamic and complex environments.

articleTitle: EAPNet: Enhanced Attention-Guided Network for Fine-Grained Semantic Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: Ground-based cloud observation is essential for meteorological research and climate monitoring. Existing methods for cloud detection and classification in whole-sky images (WSIs) often focus solely on binary segmentation (sky and cloud) or image-level classification, which perform poorly in tasks requiring the classification and segmentation of different cloud types. This paper presents an enhanced attention-guided pyramid network (EAPNet) designed to enhance the accuracy and robustness of fine-grained cloud classification in whole-sky images through deep learning techniques. The key innovations include: 1) the utilization of the pyramid spatial pooling (PSP) module to capture multi-scale contextual information; 2) the introduction of the convolutional block attention module (CBAM), which leverages an attention mechanism to enhance feature representation; and 3) an improved decoder module that enhances localization accuracy. Experimental results demonstrate that EAPNet outperforms existing mainstream methods in both cloud classification and segmentation tasks.

articleTitle: Multi-Scale Feature Fusion Model for Wheat Spike Counting
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: Predicting wheat yield based on wheat spike images is highly significant for breeding, cultivation, and agricultural production. Counting the number accurately of wheat spikes per unit area is a crucial component in monitoring yield. A novel approach utilizing a deep convolutional neural network with multi-scale feature fusion for the automatic localization and regression of wheat spike counting is proposed. Initially, the point labeling-based P2Pnet (Point-to-Point Network) is employed as the backbone to construct the basic counting framework. Furthermore, considering the variation in the size of wheat spikes, multi-scale information is preserved by extracting features from different depth feature layers of the VGG16 network. To tackle the challenge of tiny wheat spikes, a Triplet Attention mechanism is added to the multi-scale feature fusion module, facilitating the interaction of information across the channel, height, and width dimensions to prevent the loss of features from tiny objects during the learning process. Experimental results show that on the public dataset, the Mean Absolute Error (MAE) achieved by the proposed method is 13.827, which is 20.6% lower than that of the basic P2Pnet. Compared with the single-stage object detection algorithm YOLOV5, the MAE is reduced by 9.28%. Compared with the two-stage object detection algorithm Faster R-CNN, the MAE is reduced by 1.24%.

articleTitle: High Load-to-Weight Ratio and Large-Deformation Vacuum Pneumatic Actuator
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: The potential of artificial muscles is becoming increasingly evident in a number of fields, including robotics, prosthetics, and wearable devices. However，there is still a need to develop a soft actuator that is lightweight, compact and has a high load-to-weight ratio.We designed, manufactured, modeled and tested modular contracting actuators which achieves remarkable deformations exceeding 80% while supporting loads up to 4 kg. With a load-to-weight ratio of 455 and an energy conversion efficiency of 20.5% under a 1 kg load. The actuator stands out in performance. It is driven by negative pressure, offering significantly higher safety compared to actuators driven by positive pressure or other methods like electrical, thermal, or chemical means. Our fabrication process is both rapid and cost-effective. Additionally, we present a theoretical model to explain and predict the actuator's motion. Benefiting from its unprecedented modularity and high performance, this actuator is poised for practical applications in fields such as healthcare and industrial production.

articleTitle: A Rule and Network Dual-Driven Dynamic Scheduling Approach for Complex Flexible Manufacturing Job Shop
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: Traditional manually designed dispatching rules (DRs) cannot cope with the variety and rapid changes in production environments due to their inflexibility and lack of adaptability. Meanwhile, the development in manufacturing intelligence and informatization allows for storing a vast amount of scheduling data during production. Consequently, a novel approach emerges in constructing scheduling models and decision-making strategies based on historical data. Following this idea, this paper proposes a dual-driven dynamic scheduling approach for complex flexible manufacturing job shops, utilizing a combination of manually designed DRs and backpropagation neural network (BPNN) technology. Specifically, six different production scenarios are designed to optimize different objectives, simulating the actual complex manufacturing environment. Then, a real-time scheduling mapping network model is developed with the production states as input and selected DRs as output by training the BPNN. The results demonstrate the effectiveness and practicality of the proposed method in resolving dynamic scheduling issues of complex flexible manufacturing job shops, surpassing traditional manual DRs.

articleTitle: Model-Based Covert Cyber-Attack Detection for Cooling System in Data Center
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: This paper investigates a model-based covert cyber-attack detection scheme for cooling system in data center. Firstly, a state-space model of cooling system is established based on the operational principles. Then, the existence conditions of covert cyber-attack are outlined, i.e., all attacks that satisfy these conditions cannot be detected using conventional schemes. Furthermore, a residual signal at the actuator side is proposed based on the structure of attacked system, which can detect covert cyber-attack effectively. Finally, a simulation of cooling system in data center is carried out to demonstrate the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: Multi-Attention Fusion Lightweight Single Object Tracking Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: With the continuous development of mobile application platforms, balancing real-time performance and accuracy has become a major challenge for object tracking technology, especially on resource-limited mobile devices. To address these challenges, a novel tracking algorithm called NanoMViT (Nano Mobile Vision Transformer for Object Tracking) and the ECSA (Efficient Channel and Spatial Attention) multi-attention module were proposed. By optimizing the backbone network architecture, the parameters of each module were significantly reduced. The final algorithm has a parameter count of only 709.134k and MACs of only 264.127M. Compared to the baseline algorithm, the parameter count is reduced by 66.3%, and the computational load is reduced by 50.2%. To validate the algorithm's performance, comprehensive evaluations were conducted on multiple standard tracking datasets, including VOT2018, DTB70, and LaSOT. The results show that the algorithm outperforms the baseline in aspects such as rapid deformation, tracking of similar objects, and performance under complex lighting conditions. These findings demonstrate that the algorithm has high practicality and efficiency in mobile tracking applications, but further validation is required in more complex environments.

articleTitle: Flight Control of Tilt-rotor UAV with Time-varying Constraints
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: This paper proposes a flight control strategy for the tilt-rotor UAV (TUAV) in the presence of aerodynamic disturbances and state constraints. Considering the flapping motion and rotor-wing aerodynamic disturbance, the TUAV is modeled in this paper. Then, a disturbance observer is introduced to estimate the aerodynamic disturbances, enhancing the robustness of the system. Furthermore, a safe flight controller is designed based on the timevarying barrier Lyapunov function (BLF) to address the state constraints. The bounded convergences of the closed-loop error signals are ensured by Lyapunov stability theory. The simulation results verify that the proposed control algorithm can effectively ensure that the TUAV keeps the flight state in the safe range.

articleTitle: Thrust Allocation Method for Solid Attitude and Divert Control Engine
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: A thrust allocation method for a solid attitude and divert control engine, using a single combustion chamber shared by 4 divert thrusters and 6 attitude control thrusters, is proposed. Thrust allocation for multi-valve solid rocket engines is typically under-constrained due to multiple degrees of freedom and the need for precise control. To address this, we designed a distribution strategy based on the engine's operational requirements, aiming to maximize total impulse output while prioritizing attitude control thrust synthesis. This comprehensive method optimizes thrust distribution across thrusters, ensuring the engine operates within design constraints for reliable and precise control in spacecraft and missile systems. Our approach demonstrates significant improvements over traditional methods by ensuring effective thrust utilization, minimizing propellant consumption, and maintaining high precision in attitude and divert control. This paper offers a novel solution and algorithm for thrust allocation in solid attitude and divert control engines, contributing valuable advancements to aerospace propulsion systems.

articleTitle: Three-Dimensional Formation Pattern Maneuver Transformation Control for Multiple AUVs
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: This paper focuses on solving the problem of formation pattern maneuvers transformation for the multiple autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) formation system. The distributed three-dimensional affine formation maneuver control strategy is proposed to actuate a group AUVs to achieve the maneuvers, including rotation, scaling, shear, coplanarity, collineation, etc. Firstly, a novel distributed trajectory estimator is designed for each follower AUV to estimate its desired trajectory affinely localized by the leader AUVs. Then a continuous adaptive integral sliding mode controller is employed to fast and accurate track the desired trajectory acquired by the distributed trajectory estimator. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed control strategy is verified by the high-fidelity simulations.

articleTitle: Neural Network Design for the Restoration of Blurry Images Taken by the Line Inspection Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: Transmission line inspection robots have played an important role in transmission line inspection. However, the inspection robot occasionally oscillates when capturing images, resulting in blurry inspection images. This article proposes a neural network model based on the improved SRNdeblur algorithm. Firstly, we use residual dense modules (RDB) instead of residual modules to reduce lost information in the network. Secondly, the multi-loss fusion function is used to focus on the pixel differences, overall structure differences and frequency space differences between image pairs. Finally, a fuzzy image dataset PLID for power inspection robots was created. And the test results show that our proposed algorithm performs better on PSNR and SSIM compared to SRNdeblur.

articleTitle: Data Regression Prediction Based on PSO-CR-GWO Hybrid Optimized BP Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: In this paper, a hybrid optimization back propagation (BP) neural network based on Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Chaotic Random Grey Wolf Optimization (CR-GWO) is proposed and regression prediction is performed on the data. Aiming at the shortcomings of the swarm optimization algorithm such as low global search ability, poor local search accuracy and long search time, this paper develops a new hybrid optimization swarm optimization algorithm by integrating the population position update strategy in PSO algorithm and the population initialization strategy and position weight factor update strategy in CR-GWO algorithm. Meanwhile, the developed new swarm optimization algorithm is applied to data regression prediction. The data comparison results show that the accuracy of PSO-CR-GWO is improved by about 70.085% compared with GWO data regression processing; PSO-CR-GWO is improved by about 83.805% compared with CR-GWO, and PSO-CR-GWO is improved by about 54.568% compared with PSO-GWO.

articleTitle: Resilient Distributed Consensus in Multi-Agent Systems: Enhancing Transient Performance Under Communication Link Attacks
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: This article investigates the resilient cooperative output regulation (RCOR) challenge within a class of nonlinear multi-agent systems (MASs) featuring. The primary focus is on upholding predefined performance criteria, even in the face of potential communication link disruptions. This research addresses the limitations inherent in the tracking accuracy and the characteristics of the transient response of existing cooperative control methodologies for MASs, as well as the vulnerability of their communication frameworks to security threats. To this end, the paper introduces an innovative observer with prescribed performance and a robust control architecture that integrates backstepping and dynamic surface control (DSC) mechanisms, effectively mitigating the impact of communication link attacks. The theoretical robustness of the proposed control framework is substantiated through Lyapunov stability analysis, and the effectiveness is illustrated through an extensive simulation study.

articleTitle: Anomaly monitoring of distributed fiber optic sensors based on spatiotemporal features
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: In the field of railway transportation, distributed fiber optic sensors are widely used to detect external vibrations. The distributed structure causes external vibrations to simultaneously affect adjacent sensors, with varying degrees of impact. To address the signal overlap introduced by the distributed topology, we propose a hybrid model based on Deeper Graph Convolutional Networks (DeeperGCN) and CNN-Transformer for extracting spatiotemporal features. DeeperGCN is employed to analyze linear topological relationships, effectively capturing the interactions between neighboring sensors. The CNN-Transformer network is used to capture the dynamic changes of vibration signals in the temporal domain. Experimental results from 234,200 samples across five categories demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of our approach, improving the accuracy of vibration event classification.

articleTitle: A Multi-Perspective Recommendation Model Based on Knowledge Graph
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: A knowledge graph is a graph structure that represents and organizes knowledge, where nodes represent entities and edges represent the relationship between entities. The model uses the rich information in the knowledge graph, including entity properties, relationships, and semantic similarity, to improve the recommendation effect. However, the traditional knowledge graph is difficult to mine the user intention, so the recommendation effect is limited. In order to solve this problem, the MKGN model proposed in this paper transmits the collaboration signal and knowledge signal through the collaborative knowledge perception module, and then obtains the user and the project embedding through the knowledge attention mechanism; introduces the user interest into the potential vector of the interest module, builds the user-interest-item triplet, obtains the user and combines the user and the project embedding together for the final recommendation score. The model is compared with the baseline algorithm on two public datasets, and the model has better performance than the baseline algorithm model.

articleTitle: Optimization of the Yellow Corn Cleaning Process with the Implementation of a Mechanical System
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: This work optimizes the yellow corn cleaning process through the implementation of a mechanical system in a company of the food sector, for which the production processes and customer requirements have been analyzed, based on the analysis of the time taking, the examination of each process with the Ishikawa diagram and through indicators in the Pareto diagram, decisions were made to improve their production times since initially there was a daily production of only 92.84 bags/day in a daily workday of 8 hours, with a minimum requirement of 400 bags/day. Finally, after evaluating the necessary requirements and the required production, a new corn cleaning machine was implemented, which was built and verified, the new production times, in which the productivity was improved by 357 %, managing to produce 424.53 bags/day in a workday of 8 hours a day, likewise it generates an improvement of 78.13% in the production process, on the other hand, the cleaning process has been reduced by 87.38%, being the activity that took the most time for the company, secondly, the times not only decreased in a specific area but in all the corresponding processes such as, in the process of receiving raw material, humidity control, verification of species, feeding to the corn well, weighing control, sack sewing and storage.

articleTitle: Cooperative Adaptive Fault-Tolerant Formation Control for Heterogeneous Multiple Vehicles With Actuator Faults
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: This paper studies the fault-tolerant control problem for the heterogeneous vehicles formation systems consisting of multiple mobile robots and quadrotors with unknown time-varying actuator faults and external disturbances. First, the position and attitude subsystem of follower heterogeneous vehicles are considered and the heterogeneous characteristics are analyzed, and the heterogeneous vehicle formation system model is further presented. Then, the minimum-eigenvalue-based adaptive fault-tolerant control strategy is proposed, where the adaptive terms are adopted to compensate for the unknown time-varying actuator loss of effectiveness faults and bias faults and the computational complexity of adaptive estimation can be further reduced.

articleTitle: Research on Road Test Route Design Method of ADAS System Based on Fault Database and Dijkstra-CWOA
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: To solve the problem that it is difficult to obtain large fault data efficiently in Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS), a Dijkstra algorithm combining Cuckoo Search algorithm and Whale Optimization Algorithm (CWOA) is proposed, and dynamic multi-source path planning based on DijkstraCWOA algorithm is built. Based on the Dijkstra algorithm, the shortest path of the multi-source path is obtained first, so as to save manpower and material resources and improve work efficiency. Then, the Levy flight mechanism of Cuckoo Search (CS) algorithm is integrated into the Whale Optimization Algorithm (WOA), and the improved WOA is used to change the start node and end node of the path, so as to find the optimal cumulative weight path under the shortest path at different times, so as to obtain the path with the most fault data. The experimental results show that the Dijkstra-CWOA algorithm can effectively optimize the path in the range of fixed road nodes.

articleTitle: Fast-Repair RRT* : Path Planning Algorithm for Mobile Robots in Semi-static Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: Path planning algorithms have become particularly critical with the increasing demand for mobile robots to perform complex tasks, especially for automated navigation in scenes such as warehousing and logistics. In response to this need, this paper proposes a sampling-based path planning algorithm (Fast-Repair RRT*). The algorithm is designed to achieve path repair during local changes in the environment, and it does not require global path replanning. It is divided into two stages: initial path generation and path repair. First, an improved RRT* algorithm is used to generate the initial path. Then, a path repair method is introduced when the initial path is infeasible. This method is able to obtain feasible paths in a timely manner, and the path considers factors like path length, smoothness, and memory usage. Compared with other planning algorithms, Fast-Repair RRT* is able to generate higher quality initial paths. Through simulated experiments conducted in a semi-static environment, and the experiments confirmed the effectiveness and efficiency of the algorithm in path repair in such environments.

articleTitle: UAV Small Target Detection Algorithm Based on YOLOv8 Lightweight
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: Despite significant progress in the lightweight design of UAVs, the limited computational resources that can be carried, and the existence of small targets with small sizes, inconspicuous features, and susceptibility to background interference and occlusion, UAV small target detection is still challenging. To maintain a certain accuracy while significantly reducing the model size, the article proposes a small target detection algorithm based on the YOLOv8s network. Firstly, the C2f module in the Backbone part is replaced by the DynamicConv module, which introduces adaptive convolution kernel parameters to enhance the feature extraction capability while reducing the redundancy of parameters; secondly, the weighted bidirectional feature pyramid BiFPN is utilized as the Neck-end network, which operates its highly efficient feature fusion, redundancy-reducing connection and weighted feature fusion mechanisms to improves the model accuracy, reduces the number of parameters and computation in the convolution process; finally, the up-sampling method of the original model is replaced with CARAFE and the loss function is replaced with WIoU, which enhances the model's ability to extract features in small targets, and improves the mAP50% by 1.4% and reduces the model volume by 69.8% compared to the VisDrone2019 dataset. The experimental results show that the improved model can more accurately recognize small targets in aerial photography, and can greatly reduce the volume of the model while maintaining higher accuracy.

articleTitle: Design of Vision-guided Gripping System for 6DOF Robots Combined with Dexterous Hands
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: In the robot application system incorporating dexterous hand, a vision-based robot grasping system is proposed to address the lack of robustness of dexterous hand in grasping fixed attitude objects. First, a 6DOF robot grasping system based on machine vision is constructed using dexterous hand, depth camera and 6DOF collaborative robot, which realizes accurate grasping under vision guidance; second, to solve the problem of vision system's poor localization accuracy due to the loss of image information and features caused by image noise, occlusion and complex background in the process of image processing, a pooling layer and attention mechanism to enhance the feature extraction ability; moreover, an optimized dexterous hand grasping strategy is proposed through exhaustive grasping action design and analysis, which effectively improves the robustness of the system. The experimental results show that the accuracy of the target detection model reaches 87% through the localization measurement of the experimental objects, which is 2.1% higher than the original method, and the grasping success rate of the robotic system equipped with dexterous hand and depth camera is improved by 3.5%. These results validate the feasibility of the robotic grasping system incorporating dexterous hands in practical applications and significantly enhance the robustness of the system.

articleTitle: MotionGS : Compact Gaussian Splatting SLAM by Motion Filter
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: With their high-fidelity scene representation capability, the attention of SLAM field is deeply attracted by the Neural Radiation Field (NeRF) and 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS). Recently, there has been a surge in NeRF-based SLAM, while 3DGS-based SLAM is sparse. A novel 3DGS-based SLAM approach with a fusion of deep visual feature, dual keyframe selection and 3DGS is presented in this paper. Compared with the existing methods, the proposed tracking is achieved by feature extraction and motion filter on each frame. The joint optimization of poses and 3D Gaussians runs through the entire mapping process. Additionally, the coarse-to-fine pose estimation and compact Gaussian scene representation are implemented by dual keyframe selection and novel loss functions. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm not only outperforms the existing methods in tracking and mapping, but also has less memory usage.

articleTitle: Developing an Inspection Experimental System Integrating of Robot Sorting
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: Research and development of a set of integrated robot sorting inspection experimental system, the system in industrial automation, quality control, safety monitoring and other fields has a wide range of application prospects. The technical method uses a GPU-enabled TensorFlow Docker image, based on the Mask R-CNN (Mask Region-based Convolutional Neural Network) network architecture, uses the COCO (Common Objects in Context) weight file as the pre-trained deep learning model, and uses VIA (VGG Image Annotator) to label the dataset of the part of end cap of the reducer. The actual experimental results show that: the UR10 Robot is driven to pick up and handle the a single end cap part in the stacked parts to the designated location, the UR10e Robot, with on the MetraSCAN 3D scanner, is equipped with a C-Track tracker and realizes automatic inspection experimental through a programmed program. The experimental teaching application effect has also been well feedback. The research results not only provide a good research foundation for the development and application of system-related technologies, especially measurement or robotics, but also provide a reference for the integration of software and hardware resources in the laboratory.

articleTitle: Diffusion Actor with Behavior Critic Guidance Algorithm for Offline Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: To address the multimodal nature of offline dataset distributions and the overestimation problem associated with out- of-distribution (OOD) actions, this paper introduces the diffusion actor with behavior critic guidance (DABCG) algorithm. The proposed method first employs diffusion models to model the target policy, incorporating a Q-value guidance term into the actor loss to enhance the algorithm’s expressiveness while achieving performance that surpasses the behavior policy. The introduction of Q-value guidance ensures that the learned actions are directed toward higher-value regions of the action space, thus facilitating enhanced policy optimization. Furthermore, by integrating behavior critic guidance into the policy evaluation process, the algorithm effectively constrains the overestimation of OOD actions, ensuring robust performance. Experimental results on the D4RL benchmark dataset provide strong empirical evidence supporting the efficacy of the DABCG algorithm.

articleTitle: Robust Object Recognition in Open Environments Based on Causal Inference
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence technology has drawn widespread attention to the problem of target recognition in open environments. Traditional target recognition methods are easily affected by environmental changes and interference noise, leading to insufficient recognition accuracy and robustness. This paper proposes a robust target recognition method based on causal inference, aiming to improve the robust performance of image recognition models in open environments. The method first extracts features from images, analyzes the impact of noise features such as the environment in image features, and derives the essential feature properties of the target. Then, the causal relationship is introduced into the target recognition, and by analyzing the relationship between the environment, the target, and the observation data, the features of the target are combined with the observation data to achieve accurate and stable recognition of the target. The proposed method has achieved good target recognition effects on multiple open datasets, and the experimental results show that the algorithm can effectively solve the problem of poor robustness of the target recognition model in open environments, providing strong support for practical applications. Through the application of this method, the stability and robustness of the target recognition model can be significantly improved, which has important practical application value.

articleTitle: Simulation and optimization of inchworm-like pneumatic crawling actuator based on ABAQUS software
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: The actuator, serving as the fundamental power source of a soft robot, functions as its central component. The field of soft robotics has garnered increasing research attention since its inception. Pneumatic crawling robots, being an essential branch within the realm of soft robotics, possess notable characteristics such as rapid response time, cost-effectiveness, and human-computer interaction safety. Consequently, they hold significant research value. Among various types of crawling robots that have garnered considerable interest from researchers is the inchworm crawling robot. This paper aims to address the design and development aspects pertaining to inchworm actuators. By utilizing ABAQUS simulation software and taking displacement as the reference parameter, an analysis was conducted to investigate the impact of various geometric parameters on actuator displacement. Additionally, optimization of these geometric parameters was performed. The values of aspect ratio, length-to-width ratio, vertex angle and gap depth suitable for inchworm-like actuator are obtained. These findings are presented for the first time in the field of crawling soft robots and provide a theoretical basis for the development of pneumatic inchworm-like actuators.

articleTitle: Workpiece Recognition and Localization Based on Improved YOLOv7-Tiny Channel Pruning
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: At present, to address the problem of difficult detection of industrial parts and complex model with large computation, a workpiece recognition and detection algorithm based on improved YOLOv7-Tiny channel pruning is proposed. Firstly, the algorithm integrates the ECA module, an efficient channel attention mechanism, into the backbone network to better retain the information in transmission, so that the data features are more fully retained in the process of transmission, and thus the model can be optimized and the detection accuracy of the model can be improved; secondly, the lightweight up-sampling operator CARAFE is invoked to replace the nearest-neighbor difference of the original up-sampling in the structure of the PAFPN in order to improve the feature fusion ability of the model; finally, the improved model is subjected to channel pruning to reduce the number of parameters and computation of the model to further optimize the model. The experimental results show that our method achieves 81.5% recognition accuracy on the self-constructed dataset, and the number of parameters and computation amount decrease by 75.6% and 74.0%, respectively. The effectiveness of the method is proved.

articleTitle: Efficient algorithms for distributed virtual force-based self-spreading of robotic sensor/actuator networks
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: Node deployment is a key issue in building sensor/actuator networks. To improve coverage and reduce costs, the use of autonomous mobile robotic nodes is an attractive option. This paper presents two new virtual force-based (VFB) distributed self-deployment algorithms for robotic networks. Their performance is compared with the baseline behaviors of five existing cutting-edge VFB methods. This analysis is conducted using a whole lot of standard criteria: elapsed time, coverage percentage, energy consumption, mean distance, and distance uniformity. Also, we propose and use a new criterion that assesses the balance of network’s resources allocated to serve various equally valid subareas. Monte-Carlo computer experiments show that the proposed algorithms demonstrate the best performance regarding the coverage uniformity and percentage.

articleTitle: Semantic Segmentation-based Algorithm for Visual Measurement of Rotor Shaft Vibration Features
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: When detecting rotating objects, the rotating objects are usually in complex industrial environments with complex backgrounds and many interferences. Traditional visual measurement methods are difficult to effectively distinguish between the rotating object and the background, resulting in measurement errors. In this paper, a spindle is used as the image acquisition medium, and a semantic segmentation method based on deep learning is introduced to solve the difficulty of visual vibration measurement of rotating shafts. The semantic segmentation network outperforms the traditional visual measurement methods in extracting the features of rotating objects, and the network model, based on the improvement of U-Net, incorporates the improved CSimAM attention mechanism in each of the encoding and decoding stages of the bottleneck layer, which makes the network more adept at segmenting rotary axes in backgrounds with different lighting, blurring and similarity. The study in this paper not only verifies the effectiveness and superiority of the improved U-KAN network in the visual measurement of rotor shaft vibration displacement, but also provides an important theoretical and practical basis for subsequent research.

articleTitle: Coverage Path Planning for Maritime Search based on Reinforcement Learning with Path Expansion Strategy
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: In maritime search and rescue (SAR) operations, the planning of search paths directly impacts the efficiency of rescuing individuals in distress at sea. This study proposes a path-expanding reinforcement learning model designed to achieve complete coverage of maritime accident areas. Multiple scenarios are considered in conjunction with reward functions, aimed at maximizing the cumulative success rate of rescue operations within a finite time frame. The strategy allows rescue units to utilize diagonal movement to avoid redundant search efforts. Through comparative analysis, superior starting points for rescue operations are identified. The adoption of the Upper Confidence Bound (UCB) strategy within the reinforcement learning algorithm effectively reduces the likelihood of redundant search efforts and shortens path lengths. Rescue units equipped with path-expanding capabilities demonstrate higher search efficiency compared to conventional rescue path planning units. The path-expanding strategy is combined with the UCB strategy to improve the efficiency and success rate of maritime search and rescue operations through the exploration of diverse search starting points.

articleTitle: Impact of Machinery Modernization in the Peruvian Textile Industry: A Case Study of the Company Diseño y Color E.I.R.L.
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: In the textile industry, equipment modernization is crucial to increase efficiency and competitiveness. However, many companies continue to use obsolete machinery, which not only limits production capacity, but also generates additional labor costs and slows down processes. These older machines are less efficient and require more manual intervention, which increases the likelihood of errors and physical wear and tear on operators, in addition to increasing maintenance costs. The objective of this research was to evaluate the impact of replacing the SIRUBA 757 machine with the JACK DIGITAL C6-4-MO3/333 in the company Diseño y Color E.I.R.L. It was analyzed how the incorporation of this new technology, characterized by its advanced functions, lower energy consumption and reduced maintenance requirements, improved the production of T-shirts. To achieve this objective, several methodological tools were used, such as direct observation, analysis and operations diagrams, Ishikawa diagrams, time recording, and path and flow diagrams. These tools allowed a detailed evaluation of operational changes and their effects on productivity and working conditions. The results showed that the integration of modern machinery not only increased production capacity, but also significantly improved working and environmental conditions within the company. Specifically, the new machinery reduced production time in the assembly of T-shirts from 2735.52 minutes to 2129.76 minutes, representing a 22.14% improvement in efficiency. This increase in efficiency reflected the versatility and effectiveness of the JACK DIGITAL C6-4-MO3/333 compared to its predecessor.

articleTitle: Improvement Of Processes In The Mixing And Drying Of Bricks In The Company Toro S.A.C
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: Against a backdrop of projected growth in the construction market and a decline in domestic brick production in Peru, the company faces pressure to optimise its production processes. The effective implementation of humidity controls and improvements in the drying process was considered crucial to minimise the environmental impact of operations and ensure a more sustainable use of natural resources. This work aims to propose the application of precise technological controls to manage humidity and optimise the drying process in the Toro S.A.C. brick company, not only that, but also to reduce the effect on the environment and support the preservation of natural resources. Tools such as: Direct visual observation, graphic representation of the process, time recording, detailed process analysis, Ishikawa cause and effect diagram were used, which made it possible to identify problems, evaluate, investigate the causes, apply improvements and subsequently evaluate their effectiveness. After the implementation of these controls, the results showed a significant improvement in the optimisation and quality of brick manufacturing production. Variability in the amount of moisture and wastage due to brick deformation were reduced, contributing to the company’s competitive efficiency and long-term sustainable viability in the market.

articleTitle: Lightweight Tea Shoots Detection Algorithm Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: In machine tea picking, the complex tea garden environment and frequent occlusions require an algorithm that can accurately identify tea shoots while being deployable on resource-limited mobile devices. To address this, a lightweight YOLO-TD (You Only Look Once-Tea Detect) tea shoots detection algorithm based on improved YOLOv8 is proposed. The algorithm uses lightweight C2f-faster modules for feature extraction, reducing model complexity while enhancing central feature extraction capabilities. Inner-SIoU is employed as the loss function to optimize training and improve sensitivity to small tea shoots. Additionally, the G-Head structure with a dual-branch feature extraction design is used. Experimental results show that the proposed algorithm achieves a mean average precision (mAP) of 82.20%, reduces the Giga Floating-point Operations Per Second (GFLOPS) by 45.24%, accurately identifies key points of tea shoots, and effectively detects occluded tea shoots. This improved algorithm offers a robust solution for tea shoot detection in machine tea picking.

articleTitle: Cheese Production Based on Industry 4.0 automation and Simulation in the Company "Vakilact"
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: Cheese production in Peru has reached 145,765 tonnes in 2022, according to the report issued by the Agraria, on the other hand, cheese is the second most consumed dairy product, even so, in Peru much of the production is still maintained by artisanal processes which can result in fatigue and stress for workers. In addition, the lack of automation in production plants not only limits the ability to scale up production to meet growing demand, but can also affect the quality and consistency of the final product. In this context, the present research work proposes to analyse the cheese production processes in the company "Vakilact" with the aim of proposing a cheese production based on Industry 4. 0 of automation and simulation, for which an inspection of the company was carried out, to analyse the current processes, after which time was taken, to then establish the processes in sequence with the DAP, DOP, to establish the number of operations, transports, inspections, storage, distance, after which the tool of the Ishikawa diagram was used to determine the problems and causes that originate within the company, to be expressed by means of the Pareto diagram. Finally, the cheese production process was analysed, focusing on the application of advanced technologies and automated systems to ensure quality and efficiency at all stages. Key operations are detailed, from pH control and pasteurisation to pressing, ripening and storage of the cheese. Pneumatic presses, robotic arms and conveyor belts were considered, this would improve efficiency and accuracy allowing Vakilact to be more flexible and responsive to market demands, controlled from the HMI screen where we ensure quality control, resource optimisation and integration of advanced technologies to ensure excellence in cheese production.

articleTitle: Design of Sliding Mode Linear Active Disturbance Rejection Quadcopter UAV Controller based on Particle Swarm Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: To address the nonlinear, underactuated, and strongly coupled dynamics of quadrotor UAV systems, this paper proposes a control strategy. The designed controller combines sliding mode control (SMC) with linear active disturbance rejection control (LADRC) to effectively handle significant external disturbances. The controller employs a linear extended state observer (LESO) to estimate model uncertainties and external disturbances, while SMC is utilized to address the reduction in control precision caused by the bandwidth limitations of LESO. To enhance the efficiency of parameter tuning, the particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm is introduced, overcoming the inefficiencies of traditional empirical methods. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method exhibits strong disturbance rejection and fast response in altitude and attitude control of quadrotor UAVs. Compared to standalone PID control and LADRC, this approach significantly improves the attitude control performance, stability, and robustness of the quadrotor UAV.

articleTitle: Model-free control Algorithm for PMSM With Improved Adaptive Time-varying Convergence Law and New Observer
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: In order to improve the response speed and anti-interference ability of the permanent magnet synchronous motor control system, this paper proposes a model-free controller based on improved adaptive exponential convergence law and double power sliding mode observer. Firstly, the sigmoid function is used instead of the sign function to make the control signal smoother and reduce the jitter; secondly, the system state variables are introduced to form an improved adaptive exponential convergence law to enhance the response speed and anti-interference ability; finally, an improved double power sliding mode observer is designed to enhance the anti-interference ability of the system and make the disturbance observation more accurate. Simulation results show that the improved controller reduces the overshoot by 0.46% compared with the traditional method, the adjustment time of speed and torque is shortened by at least 0.01s, the three-phase current recovers the stability faster when the load is added suddenly, and the speed reaches and stabilises at the target value more rapidly when the speed increases suddenly. In summary, the control strategy proposed in this paper achieves fast response, small overshooting, shortened adjustment time, and strong anti-interference ability in static state, effectively weakening the vibration phenomenon.

articleTitle: Biomimetic Navigation of Non-holonomic Underactuated Robots for Non-gradient Based Seeking and Tracking Extended Sources
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: A robot of the Dubins-car type travels in a planar workspace that hosts an unknown scalar field. Two sensors supply the robot with the point-wise field measurements. The paper presents a new biologically inspired control strategy that drives the robot to the set of the field maximizers, with particular attention to the case where they form a whole curve. This strategy is hybrid, operates in two discrete modes, and uses sliding mode control technique. If the maximizers form a whole curve, that strategy also endows the robot with the capacity of tracking this curve. The proposed strategy is justified by a mathematically rigorous non-local convergence result and via computer simulation tests. It does not use gradient estimation and is non-demanding with respect to computation and motion.

articleTitle: Research on Self-diagnosis Method of Nickel top-Blowing Furnace Sensor Based on Causal Graph Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: As the scale of nickel top-blowing furnace melting systems expands and the complexity of the equipment increases, the maintenance workload for sensors has gradually increased. Manual maintenance approaches consume significant resources and are not suitable for the development of smart sensors. To address this issue, an unsupervised sensor self-diagnosis method is proposed in this paper. Firstly, the Pearson correlation coefficient is introduced to construct a graph network of sensors of the same type, and node embedding is used to form super nodes of sensors. Secondly, transfer entropy is utilized to assess the causal relationships between these super nodes, based on which a super node graph network is constructed. Finally, a Multi-Head Self-Attention Gated Graph Convolutional Network (MCB-GCN) is introduced. This network captures spatial and temporal dependencies of nodes and, with the help of an enhanced fusion module, achieves time-series prediction for sensors. Subsequently, sensor self-diagnosis is achieved through a standardized residual consistency check algorithm. Simulation experiments on the measurement system of a nickel top-blowing furnace demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, in addressing the problem of autonomous sensor diagnostics.

articleTitle: Efficient Kinematic Calibration for Industrial Manipulators based on a Simplified POE model
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: The Product-of-Exponential (POE) model simplifies kinematic modeling by establishing direct relationships between kinematic and end-effector errors using base coordinate and tool coordinates. However, It contains numerous parameters and high latitude, which may lead to reduced efficiency and precision in the case of limited test data. This paper introduces the Simplified Effective Kinematic Calibration (SEC) technique, combining the Simplified Product-of-Exponential (SPOE) model, Pre-processing Sequential Quadratic Programming (PSQP), and Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) to enhance calibration accuracy and efficiency. The SEC technique reduces parameter identification dimension, identifies coordinate transformation, compensates for geometric errors, and uses GPR for non-geometric error compensation. Experiments show that SEC demonstrates better positioning accuracy and efficiency than traditional methods.

articleTitle: A Brain-Inspired Approach for Compliant Force Interaction Control under Predefined Tasks
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: Force-controlled robots usually rely on preset models for interaction, and it is difficult to achieve compliant interaction without accurate environment models. In contrast, human brain can interact deftly and compliantly without a model. Therefore, this paper proposes a bionic compliant control approach based on the motor cortex-cerebellum to simulate the joint function of the human brain to control limbs for compliant interaction and improve the force compliant interaction effect of the robot when it has predefined tasks. The approach includes a motor cortex compliant trajectory planner constructed with an echo state network (ESN) and a cerebellum joint controller based on a spiking neural network (SNN). We applied and verified this approach to the simulated interactive control of a 7-DoF robotic manipulator. The results show that this approach can adaptively adjust the trajectory when performing predefined tasks, reduce the interaction force, and improve the naturalness and safety of the interaction.

articleTitle: Improved RRT*-Smart Algorithm for UGV Path Planning in Emergency Rescue Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: In emergency rescue scenarios, path planning for UGVs is a mission-critical task. However, many algorithms based on the Rapidly-exploring Random Trees (RRT) often exhibit instability and inefficiency in such scenarios. Therefore, to address the challenge of UGV path planning in emergency rescue scenarios, this paper proposes an improved version of the RRT*-Smart algorithm named TAD-RRT*-Smart. The improvement of the proposed algorithm mainly involves three aspects: First, a target point attraction module is introduced, which integrates APF to make the random tree oriented during expansion, thus accelerating the convergence rate. Second, a dynamic step size adjustment module is introduced, which enhances the adaptability of UGV in different environments. Finally, the tree node expansion process is refined, which enhances the expansion efficiency of the intelligent sampling and the ability to pass through complex areas. The simulation experiments show that the TAD-RRT*-Smart algorithm exhibits outstanding optimal path quality and stability in various environments, as well as superior initial path generation capability. Thus, it can provide a reliable answer for UGV path planning in emergency rescue scenarios.

articleTitle: Productivity Increase in the Production Line in the Recharge of Fire Extinguishers Based on Industry 4.0
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Robotics, Control and Automation Engineering (RCAE)
abstract: Fire extinguisher recharging and fire control using dry chemical powder (DPC) are crucial practices globally, especially in view of the alarming increase in fires and the imperative need for operational and effective fire extinguishers. These devices, essential for safety, have an expiry date that makes their periodic maintenance mandatory. In Peru, the companies responsible for recharging fire extinguishers operate under the Peruvian Technical Standard NTP 350.043-1. However, many of these companies carry out the recharging process manually, exposing workers to the risks of handling PQS, a substance harmful to health. In addition, manual procedures are repetitive and susceptible to human error, highlighting the need and potential for adopting advanced technologies to improve efficiency and safety in these processes. The research work focuses on the improvement of the PQS fire extinguisher recharging production line based on Industry 4.0 of the company "Fumisem S.A. C", for which it was necessary to know the processes that perform through a visit, in which a study of times by means of chronometer was made, then to establish the diagram of route, the Diagram of operations of the Process (DOP), The Analytical Diagram of the Process (DAP), which were key to establish the operations, inspections, inputs for each process, likewise the productivity and the unproductivity was seen, on the basis of it the industry 4. 0 where a plant is simulated to scale of the operation of the recharge of fire extinguishers, which was made based on all the requirements and processes described in this work, likewise this work raises the elimination of manpower which will be replaced by industrial automation, on the other hand this type of approach is efficient because the machines do not perform unnecessary movements which improves productivity and times in the recharge of fire extinguishers.
